自动生成的描述、内容源自引用的AUTOSAR-R25-11文档（SWS规范和随附的标准文档）——不是正式的AUTOSAR文本。标记为解释的陈述是从来源得出的结论。

Rolle & Verwendungszweck

Der Functional Cluster Platform Health Management (ara::phm) überwacht das korrekte zeitliche und logische Ausführungsverhalten von Prozessen und Softwarekomponenten auf der AUTOSAR Adaptive Plattform SWS Platform Health Management §1 “Introduction and functional overview”. Als zentrale Sicherheits- und Zuverlässigkeitsinstanz stellt PHM sicher, dass Rechenzeitüberschreitungen, Programmabstürze, Endlosschleifen oder fehlerhafte Kontrollflüsse frühzeitig erkannt und durch deterministische Recovery-Maßnahmen oder Hardware-Watchdog-Eskalationen abgefangen werden [SWS_PHM_00101].

Das Modul aggregiert lokale Kontrollpunktmeldungen von sogenannten Supervised Entities, bewertet diese anhand formal modellierter Überwachungsregeln und leitet bei Abweichungen abgestufte Reaktionen ein. Hierzu gehören die Benachrichtigung der betroffenen Anwendung oder des State Managements zur Initiierung von Wiederanläufen oder Funktionsgruppenwechseln sowie bei kritischen Systemfehlern die Ansteuerung physischer Watchdogs [SWS_PHM_00231] [SWS_PHM_01229].

Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge

Die Architektur von ara::phm trennt strikt zwischen der Instrumentierung in den Anwendungs-Prozessen und der zentralen Auswertungslogik im PHM-Dämon SWS Platform Health Management §7 “Functional specification”:

  • Supervised Entity (ara::phm::SupervisedEntity): Repräsentiert ein softwaremäßiges Überwachungsobjekt (z. B. einen Prozess, einen Thread oder eine kritische Funktionsschleife). Die Anwendung instanziiert SupervisedEntity über einen im Manifest definierten InstanceSpecifier und meldet das Erreichen von Kontrollpunkten über ReportCheckpoint(checkpointId) [SWS_PHM_00104] [SWS_PHM_00425]. Diese Aufrufe sind lock-frei und minimalinvasiv gestaltet, um deterministisches Laufzeitverhalten zu gewährleisten.
  • Drei Überwachungsmechanismen (Elementary Supervisions): PHM bewertet Checkpoints anhand dreier komplementärer Kriterien:
    • Alive Supervision: Prüft, ob ein Checkpoint innerhalb eines definierten Referenzzeitraums mit einer erwarteten Mindest- und Höchstfrequenz gemeldet wird (Erkennung von Thread-Blockaden oder unkontrolliertem Durchlaufen) [SWS_PHM_01123].
    • Deadline Supervision: Misst die Latenzzeit zwischen zwei definierten Checkpoints (z. B. Beginn und Ende einer Bildverarbeitungsroutine) und detektiert Fristüberschreitungen oder unzulässig frühe Ausführungen [SWS_PHM_01127].
    • Logical Supervision: Verifiziert die Einhaltung eines zulässigen Kontrollflussgraphen (Transitionen zwischen Checkpoints), um unzulässige Sprünge oder übersprungene Initialisierungen abzufangen [SWS_PHM_01141].
  • Status-Aggregation & Funktionsgruppen-Kontext: Jede elementare Überwachung besitzt einen lokalen Elementary Supervision Status. Diese werden innerhalb eines Function-Group-Kontexts über ein Worst-of-Prinzip zu einem Global Supervision Status verdichtet [SWS_PHM_00216] [SWS_PHM_00218]. Befindet sich eine Funktionsgruppe im Zustand NoSupervision, werden eingehende Checkpoints ignoriert [SWS_PHM_01142].
  • Recovery Action (ara::phm::RecoveryAction): Schnittstelle zur Entkopplung von Fehlererkennung und Fehlerreaktion. Registrierte Handler empfangen Benachrichtigungen bei Zustandsübergängen auf kEXPIRED und leiten Wiederanläufe oder Fallback-Betriebsmodi ein [SWS_PHM_01333].

Interaktionsfluss

Der Interaktionsfluss beginnt mit dem Melden von Kontrollpunkten durch die Supervised Entity. PHM aktualisiert intern die Zähler, Zeitstempel und Graphzustände. Solange alle Prüfungen innerhalb der Toleranzbänder liegen, verbleibt der Globalstatus in kOK. Bei einer Verletzung wechselt der Status auf kFAILED bzw. nach Ablauf konfigurierter Fehlertoleranzen auf kEXPIRED, was den Recovery-Handler aktiviert. Führt dies zu keiner Wiederherstellung oder betrifft der Fehler das Basis-Betriebssystem bzw. Execution Management, wechselt der Status auf kSTOPPED und löst die Watchdog-Eskalation aus.

Interaktionsdiagramm: Zyklische Checkpoint-Meldung durch eine Supervised Entity, interne Bewertung (Alive/Deadline/Logical), Benachrichtigung der RecoveryAction bei Statusübergang nach kEXPIRED und abschließende Watchdog-Eskalation bei anhaltendem kSTOPPED. Quellen: [SWS_PHM_00425], [SWS_PHM_00231] und [SWS_PHM_01229].

Konfiguration & Fehlerbehandlung

Die Parametrierung erfolgt deklarativ im AUTOSAR-Manifest über PlatformHealthManagementContribution. Dort werden Checkpoints, Zeitschranken (Min/Max-Deadlines in Mikrosekunden), Alive-Toleranzzyklen, zulässige Graphübergänge sowie die Zuordnung von Supervised Entities zu Function Groups konfiguriert SWS Platform Health Management §7.4 “Determination of Supervision Status”.

Die Zustandsmaschine des Global Supervision Status unterscheidet fünf deterministische Zustände [SWS_PHM_00216]:

  • kDEACTIVATED: Die Überwachung ist für die aktuelle Funktionsgruppe nicht aktiv.
  • kOK: Alle elementaren Überwachungen erfüllen ihre Spezifikationsgrenzen.
  • kFAILED: Mindestens eine Überwachung hat einen Fehler detektiert, befindet sich aber noch innerhalb der konfigurierten Fehlertoleranzschwelle (z. B. einzelne ausgelassene Alive-Meldung).
  • kEXPIRED: Die Fehlertoleranz wurde überschritten; die Überwachung ist abgelaufen. Dieser Zustand löst unmittelbar die hinterlegte RecoveryAction aus [SWS_PHM_00231].
  • kSTOPPED: Terminaler Fehlerzustand, wenn Recovery-Maßnahmen fehlschlagen oder Kernprozesse (EM/OS) betroffen sind. In diesem Zustand wird der Hardware-Watchdog nicht mehr getriggert, was einen kontrollierten System-Reset einleitet [SWS_PHM_01229].

# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P8_08",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis document is the software specification of the\nPlatform Health Management\nfunctional cluster within the Adaptive Platform [1].\nThe specification implements the requirements specified in [2, RS Platform Health\nManagement].\nIt also implements the general functionality described in the Foundation documents [3,\nRS Health Monitoring] and [4, ASWS Health Monitoring]. In addition to the functionality\nspecified in [4], this document also defines\nHealth Channel Supervision\n.\nHealth Monitoring\nis required by [5, ISO 26262:2018] (under the terms control flow\nmonitoring, external monitoring facility, watchdog, logical monitoring, temporal moni-\ntoring, program sequence monitoring) and this specification is supposed to address all\nrelevant requirements from this standard.\n8 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P9_09",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 9,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to the specification\nor implementation of\nHealth Monitoring\nthat are not included in the [6, AUTOSAR\nglossary]."
    },
    {

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_11",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\n[1] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Design\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign\n[2] Requirements on Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_PlatformHealthManagement\n[3] Requirements on Health Monitoring\nAUTOSAR_FO_RS_HealthMonitoring\n[4] Specification of Health Monitoring\nAUTOSAR_FO_ASWS_HealthMonitoring\n[5] ISO 26262:2018 (all parts)  Road vehicles  Functional Safety\nhttps://www.iso.org\n[6] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[7] General Specification of Basic Software Modules\nAUTOSAR_CP_SWS_BSWGeneral\n[8] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[9] Specification of State Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement\n[10] Specification of Execution Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement\n[11] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[12] Specification of Intrusion Detection System Manager for Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_IntrusionDetectionSystemManager\n[13] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\n[14] Guidelines for using Adaptive Platform interfaces\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines\n3.2 Further applicable specification\nAUTOSAR provides a general specification [7, SWS_BSWGeneral] which is also appli-\ncable for\nPlatform Health Management\n. The specification SWS General shall be\n11 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_12",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nconsidered as additional and required specification for implementation of\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n.\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [8] which is also applicable for\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n. The chapter \"General requirements for all FunctionalClusters\"\nof this specification shall be considered as an additional and required specification for\nimplementation of\nPlatform Health Management\n.\n12 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P13_13",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Known limitations\n•\nDaisy chaining\n(i.e. forwarding Supervision Status,\nCheckpoint\nor\nHealth\nChannel\ninformation to an entity external to PHM or another PHM instance) is\ncurrently not supported in this document release.\n•\nInterface with the Diagnostic Manager is not specified in this release.\n•\nHealth Channels\n(HealthChannelExternalStatus) is set to obsolete.\nNote: It is not intended to remove this feature from\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Plat-\nform\noverall. Rather, it is an architectural question to which Functional Cluster\nthis feature belongs to, that is expected to be resolved for the next release.\n•\nThe configuration attribute for the alive notification cycle time (with respect to\nPHM sending AliveNotification to watchdog interface) is not specified for this re-\nlease.\n•\nA change in the value of Supervision (Alive/Deadline/Logical) configuration pa-\nrameters between two\nFunction Group\nstates wherein the process being su-\npervised continues to execute on switching between these states is not con-\nsidered. The Supervision continues as per configuration in the\nSupervision\nMode\ncorresponding to old\nFunction Group\nstate.\n•\nSimilar to above limitation, dynamic change between Supervision exclusion (dis-\nable) and Supervision inclusion (enable) on\nFunction Group\nstate change\nwherein the process under consideration continues to execute on change in\nFunction Group\nstate is not supported. Supervision exclusion or inclusion\ncan be applied starting with the\nFunction Group\nstate in which execution of\nthe process begins and the same is applied until termination of the process.\n•\nCurrently specified mechanism of Notifying State Management on\nGlobal Su-\npervision Status\nreaching state\nkStopped\nis insufficient in case of multiple\nfailures. It could happen that the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nremains in\nstate\nkStopped\nwithout further notification to State Management about succes-\nsive failures. Thereby the recovery might be hindered.\n•\n\"PowerMode\" dependent Supervision configuration is not supported in this re-\nlease. See [9] for information on \"PowerMode\".\n•\nSupervision is not supported for non-reporting processes (for information regard-\ning what is a non-reporting process, please refer [10]). Rationale: Supervision\ndepends on process states. Non-reporting process is not expected to report its\nExecution State to Execution Management. Hence,\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\ncannot be informed about the necessary process states by Execution\nManagement.\n•\nHandling of multiple hardware watchdog instances is up to implementation and\nnot standardized in the specification.\n13 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P14_14",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\nState machine of\nElementary Supervision Status\nis not specified for in-\nter process supervisions (inter process\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical\nSupervision\n) in this release.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nNo restriction\n14 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P15_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters in\nthe AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the interfaces\nprovided by\nPlatform Health Management\nto other Functional Clusters. Section\n5.2 Required Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [11].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P15_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.1: Interfaces provided by Platform Health Management to other Functional Clus-\nters\nFigure 5.1 shows interfaces provided by\nPlatform Health Management\nto other\nFunctional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Table 5.1 provides a com-\nplete list of interfaces provided to other Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adap-\ntive Platform."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P15_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Diagnostic Management\nshould use this interface to\nenable supervision of its daemon process(es) by\nPlatform Health Management\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_18",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_19",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.2: Interfaces required by Platform Health Management from other Functional\nClusters\nFigure 5.2 shows the interfaces required by\nPlatform Health Management\nfrom\nother Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Table 5.2 provides a\ncomplete list of required interfaces from other Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_20",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Platform Health Management\nuses this interface to\nreport the state of its daemon process to\nExecution\nManagement\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_21",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Platform Health Management\nshall use this interface\nto log standardized messages."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_22",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Platform Health Management\nuses this interface to\ntrigger failure recovery."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P17_23",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5.3 Additional dependencies on Execution Management\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nfunctional cluster is dependent on the Execu-\ntion Management Interface [10].\nFollowing process state information is needed from Execution Management with re-\nspect to processes for which supervision is configured:\n•\nprocess reporting Execution State\nkRunning\n,\n•\nprocess terminated,\n•\nprocess is about to be informed by Execution Management to terminate.\n17 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {

      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01240",

Please note that if column Satisfied by is empty for a specific require-\nment this means that this requirement is not fulfilled by this document."

      "verbatim_text": "Platform Health Management\nshall support multiple occurrences of\nthe same Supervised Entity."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P21_57",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00457",

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P21_58",

    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P21_59",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00457",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_PHM_00457] [SWS_PHM_01118]\n[SWS_PHM_01119] [SWS_PHM_01122]\n[SWS_PHM_01128] [SWS_PHM_01129]\n[SWS_PHM_01221] [SWS_PHM_01222]\n[SWS_PHM_01223] [SWS_PHM_01224]\n[SWS_PHM_01225] [SWS_PHM_01328]\n[SWS_PHM_01329] [SWS_PHM_01330]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P22_60",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\n7.1 General description\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nmonitors applications with respect to tim-\ning constraints (\nAlive Supervision\nand\nDeadline Supervision\n) and logical\nprogram sequence (\nLogical Supervision\n) as well as platform health (\nHealth\nChannel Supervision\n). In case of a detected failure,\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\nnotifies State Management. As coordinator of the platform, State Manage-\nment can decide how to handle the error and trigger a suitable recovery action.\nPlatform Health Management has also an interface to the hardware watchdog and can\ntrigger a watchdog reaction in case of a critical failure where a notification to State\nManagement is not sufficient.\nAll the algorithms and the procedures for the\nPlatform Health Management\nare\ndescribed in the Autosar Foundation document [4] and are not specified here: only the\nAutosar Adaptive specificities, including the interfaces with the other functional clusters,\nare shown here below.\nThe interfaces of Health Management to other Functional Clusters are only informative\nand are not standardized.\n7.2 Supervision of Supervised Entities\nState Management coordinates the platform through Function Groups [9]. Within a\nFunction Group, there may be multiple\nProcesses\nrunning.\nPlatform Health Management\nmonitors\nSupervised Entitys\n. Each\nSuper-\nvised Entity\nmaps to whole or part of a\nProcess\n. The monitoring is active as long\nas the corresponding\nProcess\nis active.\nPlatform Health Management\nprovides three kinds of supervisions to monitor\na\nSupervised Entity\n:\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\n. The supervision algorithms are described in [4]. Only de-\ntails specific for Adaptive Platform are described in this document.\nThe results of the supervisions of a\nSupervised Entity\nInstance are reflected in\nthe\nElementary Supervision Status\n.There exists one\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\nper Alive, Deadline, Logical Supervision. The status of elemen-\ntary supervisions within a\nFunction Group\nis conglomerated in the corresponding\nGlobal Supervision Status\n.\nOne\nElementary Supervision Status\ncontributes to only one\nGlobal Super-\nvision Status\n. Which\nElementary Supervision Status\ncontributes to which\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis determined by to which Global Supervision the\ncorresponding supervision belongs to in the Manifest.\n22 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P23_61",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nScope of Global Supervision: Global Supervision corresponds to whole or part of a\nFunction Group\n. A Global Supervision can contain all or a certain set of Elementary\nSupervisions corresponding to processes controlled within a single Function Group\ncontext. The mapping from Supervisions to Global Supervision is flexible. Through\nconfiguration, user can decide which Supervisions belong to which Global Supervision.\nBut there are following restrictions:\n•\nall Supervisions comprising a Global Supervision are corresponding to processes\ncontrolled within a single Function Group context and\n•\na Supervision can be part of only one Global Supervision."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P24_62",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 24,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P25_63",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01341",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 25,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1. Supervisions corresponding to Processes C and D are part of a Global Supervi-\nsion GS_2 since then the Global Supervision would span across multiple\nFunc-\ntion Groups\n.\n2. Logical Supervision LogicalSup_1 corresponding to Process A is part of two\nGlobal Supervisions GS_1 and GS_2.\nAs described in [4], the supervisions are based on checkpoints which are reported by\nthe\nSupervised Entity\nInstance.\n[SWS_PHM_01341]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting of Supervision Checkpoint mapped to\nNo Supervision provision\n⌈\nIf a\nSupervisionCheckpoint\nreported to\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nvia\nReportCheckpoint\nis\n•\nconfigured to (referenced in)\nNoCheckpointSupervision\nor\n•\nthe corresponding\nSupervised Entity\ninstance is configured to\nNoSupervi-\nsion\nin the\nSupervision Mode\ncorresponding to the\nFunction Group\nState in which the\nprocess is executing, then\nPlatform Health Management\nshall ignore the report-\ning of the\nSupervisionCheckpoint\nfor evaluation of supervisions (Alive, Deadline\nand Logical).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254)\nNote: The behavior in case of reported, undefined checkpoints is currently not speci-\nfied. This will be specified in the next release.\n[SWS_PHM_01229]\n{DRAFT}\nRestricted access on reporting of Checkpoints\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall ignore the execution of\nReportCheckpoint\nfor evaluation of Alive, Deadline and Logical Supervision if the reporting process does\nnot correspond to the reported\nSupervisionCheckpoint\n, i.e. reporting process is\nnot the same as reported\nSupervisionCheckpoint\n.\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00101,\nRS_HM_09254, RS_PHM_00118)\nExample: Consider\nSupervisionCheckpoint\nSV_CP_A is referencing Process\nProc_A through attribute\nSupervisionCheckpoint\n.\nprocess\nin the manifest and it\nis referenced in\nAliveSupervision\nthrough attribute\nAliveSupervision\n.\ncheck-\npoint\n. In runtime, if a process other than Proc_A (e.g: Proc_B) reports SV_CP_A,\nthen this reporting is not to be considered for evaluation of\nAlive Supervision\n.\nIf a checkpoint is reported by the \"`wrong\"' process, this is considered as access viola-\ntion and a potential security threat.\n[SWS_PHM_01339]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting access violation w.r.t. checkpoints\nto IdsM\n⌈\nIf it occurs that the reported\nSupervisionCheckpoint\ndoes not\ncorrespond to the process reporting it, i.e. reporting process is not the\nsame as reported\nSupervisionCheckpoint\n.\nprocess\n, THEN Security event\nSEV_ACCESSVIOLATION_PHM_CHECKPOINT\ndefined in in [SWS_PHM_01340] shall\nbe reported to IdsM (see [12]) with the following context data:\n•\nIdentity of the process which is violating the access permissions\n25 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P26_64",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01340",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\nFunction Group State in which process is executing when there is this violation\n•\nWhich\nSupervisionCheckpoint\nis getting reported\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00119)\n[SWS_PHM_01340] Security events for PHM\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P26_65",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01340",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n7.2.1 Start and Stop of Supervisions\n[SWS_PHM_01331]\n{DRAFT}\nStart of Alive Supervision\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nshall start the first\naliveReferenceCycle\nof a configured\nAliveSu-\npervision\nof a\nSupervised Entity\nInstance as soon as the corresponding pro-\ncess reports Execution State\nkRunning\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_09249)\nRationale: Cyclic execution is expected only after process reached state\nkRunning\n.\nExecution Management monitors that the process reaches state\nkRunning\nwithin a\nconfigured timeout.\nThe information of process reporting Execution state\nkRunning\nis to be provided by\nExecution Management. through a vendor specific Inter Functional Cluster Interface.\n[SWS_PHM_01332]\n{DRAFT}\nCheckpoints corresponding to Alive Supervision be-\nfore kRunning\n⌈\nWith respect to\nAlive Supervision\n,\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\nshall ignore\nCheckpoints\nreported by a\nSupervised Entity\nInstance\nbefore the corresponding process reaches state\nkRunning\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_-\nHM_09249)\nImplementation hint: The same time base should be used between Execution Man-\nagement and\nPlatform Health Management\nto synchronize the\nkRunning\nstate\nwith the start of the Alive Supervision. See [SWS_PHM_01334] for details.\nNote: The start of intra-process\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervi-\nsion\n(i.e. Logical and Deadline Supervision with all referenced\nSupervisionCheck-\npoint\ns corresponding to a single process) does not depend on the process reporting\nExecution State\nkRunning\n. That is, the\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical\nSupervision\ncan start even before the process reaching state\nkRunning\n. Please\nrefer [4] for details of\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01333]\n{DRAFT}\nTermination of Supervised Processes\n⌈\nAs soon as\nPlatform Health Management\nreceives the information from Execution Manage-\nment that a supervised process is about to be notified to terminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n) or the process is terminated (considering the case of process terminat-\ning abruptly, i.e. without\nSIGTERM\nissued by Execution Management),\nPlatform\n26 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P27_66",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nHealth Management\nshall stop all intra-process supervisions corresponding to the\nprocess (that is stop all Alive, Deadline and Logical Supervision involving\nSupervi-\nsionCheckpoint\ns of the corresponding process only).\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_-\n09249)\nRationale: Process is expected to start terminating on receiving\nSIGTERM\nfrom Exe-\ncution Management. Execution Management monitors the termination timeout once\nit issues\nSIGTERM\nto the process. Considering this, additional monitoring of the pro-\ncess by\nPlatform Health Management\nvia Supervisions is considered to be not\nnecessary.\n[SWS_PHM_01334]\n{DRAFT}\nTime Source for Supervisions\n⌈\nAll timing aspects re-\nlated to\nPlatform Health Management\nshall be measured in the context of the\nreporting process using the same time source.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09254, RS_HM_09249)\nTo avoid effect of delays and jitter in the inter-process communication to\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n, timing aspects related to\nPlatform Health Management\n(i.e. synchronization of\nkRunning\nstate between Execution Management and\nPlat-\nform Health Management\n, the timestamp w.r.t reporting of checkpoints (consider\nDeadline Supervision)) shall be taken in the context of the reporting process using the\nsame time source.\nImplementation Hint:\nara::core::SteadyClock\ncould be used to obtain time\nstamp (in other words, for time keeping).\n7.2.1.1 Stopping of Alive Supervision for Self Terminating Process\nIn case of a Self-Terminating Process, the process can intentionally terminate even\nwithout\nSIGTERM\nbeing issued by Execution Management. Hence, it is necessary to\nmark the point in time at which the process starts to (self-) terminate so that the\nAlive\nSupervision\ncould be stopped. This is intended to be achieved by process reporting\na checkpoint named as\nterminatingCheckpoint\n. Additionally, a timeout (config-\nurable) has to be monitored by\nPlatform Health Management\nto check that the\nprocess terminates within this duration since reporting of\nterminatingCheckpoint\n.\nThis timeout check is to monitor that the process is not stuck in its execution and there-\nfore is not terminating.\nNote: Unless\nSIGTERM\nis issued to the process by Execution Management, Execution\nManagement will not monitor for process termination timeout.\nPlatform Health Management\nis to be informed by Execution Management re-\ngarding the termination of the process.\n[SWS_PHM_01335]\n{DRAFT}\nStopping of Alive Supervision for Self-Terminating\nProcess\n⌈\nIn case of Self-Terminating Process,\nAlive Supervision\nshall be\nstopped on reporting of\nterminatingCheckpoint\nby the process or as soon as\nPlatform Health Management\nreceives the information from Execution Manage-\n27 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P28_67",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nment that the process will be notified to terminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n), whichever is\nearlier.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_09249)\n[SWS_PHM_01336]\n{DRAFT}\nTimeout monitoring for termination of Self-\nTerminating Process\n⌈\nOn reporting of\nterminatingCheckpoint\nby a Self-\nTerminating Process,\nPlatform Health Management\nshall start monitoring the\ntimeout. That is,\nPlatform Health Management\nshall monitor that the process ter-\nminates within\nterminatingCheckpointTimeoutUntilTermination\nsince re-\nporting of\nterminatingCheckpoint\n. In case the process takes longer than\nter-\nminatingCheckpointTimeoutUntilTermination\nfor termination, this shall be\nnotified as failure to State Management.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_09249)\n[SWS_PHM_01337]\n{DRAFT}\nUnintended termination of Self-Terminating Pro-\ncess\n⌈\nIf an\nAlive Supervision\nis configured for a Self Terminating Process\nand if the process terminates without reporting\nterminatingCheckpoint\nand\nno\nSIGTERM\nwas issued to the process by Execution Management, then\nPlat-\nform Health Management\nshall notify a failure of\nAlive Supervision\nto State\nManagement via\nara::phm::RecoveryAction::RecoveryHandler\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_-\n09125, RS_HM_09249)\n[SWS_PHM_01338]\n{DRAFT}\nAvoid redundant Monitoring of Termination for Self-\nTerminating Process\n⌈\nIf an\nAlive Supervision\nis configured for a Self Terminat-\ning Process and if after reporting of\nterminatingCheckpoint\nand before\ntermi-\nnatingCheckpointTimeoutUntilTermination\nis elapsed\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nreceives the information from Execution Management that the process\nwill be notified to terminate via\nSIGTERM\n, then\nPlatform Health Management\nshall stop monitoring the timeout.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_09249)\nThis is because, once\nSIGTERM\nis issued by Execution Management to the process,\nExecution Management will monitor the process termination timeout.\n7.2.2 Supervision of processes started before Platform Health Management\nStart of Supervision (\nAlive Supervision\n/\nDeadline Supervision\n/\nLogical\nSupervision\n) in case of processes that are started before\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nprocess (e.g, process corresponding to Execution Management) is not\nstandardized. It is up to Adaptive Platform Vendor specific decision.\n7.3 Health Channel Supervision\nUsing\nHealth Channel Supervision\nthe system integrator can hook external su-\npervision results to the\nPlatform Health Management\n. External supervision can\nbe routines like RAM test, ROM test, kernel status, voltage monitoring etc. The ex-\nternal supervision performs the monitoring and debouncing. The determined result is\n28 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P29_68",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00010",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nclassified according to the possible\nHealth Status\nvalues and sent to\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n.\nA\nHealth Channel\ncan be\n•\nthe Global supervision status of the software under supervision.\n•\nthe result of an environment monitoring algorithm. e.g. Voltage Monitoring, Tem-\nperature Monitoring.\n•\nthe result of a memory integrity test routine, e.g. RAM test, ROM test.\n•\nthe status of the operating system or Kernel. e.g. OS Status, Kernel Status.\n•\nthe status of another platform instance or Virtual Machine or ECU.\nThe various external monitoring routines shall report their result or status in the form of\ndefined\nHealth Statuses\nto the\nPlatform Health Management\n. The\nHealth\nStatus\nof a\nHealth Channel\nis the abstract format of the information that a\nHealth\nChannel\nprovides to the\nPlatform Health Management\n. Two different\nHealth\nChannels\nmay have same\nHealth Status\nnames to represent its result, e.g. high,\nlow, normal.\nIf a reaction on a determined\nHealth Status\nis necessary,\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nreports the status to State Management.\n7.3.1 Health Status after Initialization\nThe\nHealth Status\nafter initialization is controlled by the configuration container\nHealthStatusInitValue\n. This parameter may be configured once for each\nHealth Channel\nin the configuration.\n[SWS_PHM_00010]\n{OBSOLETE}\nNot initialized Health Channel\n⌈\nIf the container\nHealthStatusInitValue\ndoes not exist or the\nHealth Channel\ndoes not already\nhave an initial value, the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall treat the correspond-\ning\nHealth Status\nas undefined and not use it until the corresponding\nHealth\nChannel\nhas been updated for the first time.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_09255, RS_HM_09249)\n7.3.2 Configuration of Health Channel\nA\nHealth Channel\nhas the following configuration options:\n1.\nName\n: Globally unique name identifier, used by Applications.\n2.\nID\n: Globally unique identifier (number)\n3.\nHealthStatusInitValue\n: Initial value of the corresponding Health Status.\nA\nHealth Status\nrepresents a possible value of the\nHealth Channel\nand has the\nfollowing options:\n29 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P30_69",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01328",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 30,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1.\nName\n: used by Applications, unique within the\nHealth Channel\n2.\nID\n: Identifier of the\nHealth Status\n, unique within the\nHealth Channel\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P30_70",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01328",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 30,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3:\nHealth Channel\nconfiguration\n7.3.3 Reporting of Health Channel\nThe current\nHealth Status\nis reported to\nPlatform Health Management\nvia the\nmethod\nReportHealthStatus\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01328]\n{OBSOLETE}\nConsistency of Health Status Identifier\n⌈\nThe\nvalue of\nhealthStatusId\nreported via\nReportHealthStatus\nshall match the de-\nclared\nstatusId\nof the respective\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\n.\nstatus\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nPHM_00102, RS_PHM_09257)\n[SWS_PHM_01329]\n{OBSOLETE}\nReporting of undefined Health Status Identifier\n⌈\nIf a\nhealthStatusId\nis reported to\nPlatform Health Management\nand no cor-\nresponding\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\nis configured in the context of the reporting\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\n, PHM shall ignore the reporting of healthStatus.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00102, RS_PHM_09257)\n[SWS_PHM_01330]\n{OBSOLETE}\nRestricted access on reporting of Health Status\n⌈\nThe execution of\nReportHealthStatus\nshall be prevented (i.e, shall not be con-\nsidered for notifying State Management) if the reporting process is not the same as\nthe reported\nHealthChannelExternalStatus\n.\nprocess\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00102, RS_-\nPHM_09257)\n7.4 Supervision Modes\nExpected execution (timing or sequence) of the Software can change based on certain\nconditions. Hence, the value of the Supervision (Alive/Deadline/Logical) parameters\nmight have to be changed based on conditions. For each such condition a mode called\na\nSupervision Mode\ncan be configured. Currently, this condition can be configured\nbased on\nFunction Group\nState.\n30 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P31_71",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00240",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 31,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: It is possible to exclude (disable) Supervision for a\nSupervised Entity\nIn-\nstance in a\nSupervision Mode\n. This can be achieved by configuring\nNoSupervi-\nsion\nfor the\nSupervised Entity\nInstance in the\nSupervision Mode\n.\n7.4.1 Effect of changing Mode\nIn\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n,\nSupervision Mode\nchanges on\nFunction\nGroup\nState change.\nFunction Group State change has following impact on processes:\n•\nCertain processes are terminated.\n•\nCertain processes are newly started.\n•\nCertain processes are restarted.\n•\nRemaining processes continue to execute.\nSupervisions (Alive, Deadline and Logical) of the\nSupervised Entitys\ncorrespond-\ning to the processes shall be handled as follows.\n[SWS_PHM_00240]\n{DRAFT}\nSupervisions on termination of process\n⌈\nAlive\nSupervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\nshall be\nstopped on termination of the corresponding process. Results of Alive, Deadline and\nLogical Supervision shall be set to correct.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\nThe termination of the process could be due to various reasons. It could be due to\nchange in\nFunction Group\nState (the process is not configured to be executed in\nthe new\nFunction Group\nState), a self-terminating process is terminating on its own\nor abrupt termination of a process (e.g. due to out of bound memory access).\nNote:\n1. On termination of process,\nElementary Supervision Status\nof the corre-\nsponding\nSupervised Entity\nInstance will be set to\nkDEACTIVATED\n.\n2. For a process, monitoring is active when the process is executing (that is, when\nthe Execution state of the process is \"Initializing\" or \"Running\" or \"Terminating\").\nIt is deactivated (stopped) when the process is terminated.\n[SWS_PHM_00241]\n{DRAFT}\nSupervisions on Start of Process\n⌈\nOn start of the\nprocess for which a Supervision (\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand/or\nLogical Supervision\n) is configured in the new\nFunction Group\nState,\nthe Supervision (\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand/or\nLogi-\ncal Supervision\n) shall be performed as per the configured Supervision parameter\nvalues in the\nSupervision Mode\ncorresponding to new\nFunction Group\nState.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\n[SWS_PHM_00244]\n{DRAFT}\nNoSupervision on Start of Process\n⌈\nOn start of the\nprocess in the new\nFunction Group\nState, if\nNoSupervision\nis configured for\n31 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_72",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00242",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\na\nSupervised Entity\nInstance corresponding to the process in the\nSupervi-\nsion Mode\ncorresponding to the new\nFunction Group\nState, then no Supervi-\nsion (no\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nor\nLogical Supervi-\nsion\n) shall be performed for the\nSupervised Entity\nInstance in the\nSupervision\nMode\ncorresponding to new\nFunction Group\nState.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\nNote: Even though it is supported to exclude (disable) Supervision in a particular\nSupervision Mode\n, dynamic change between Supervision inclusion (enable) and\nexclusion (disable) during execution of Process is not supported. Supervision exclusion\ncan be applied starting from the\nSupervision Mode\ncorresponding to the\nFunction\nGroup\nstate in which the execution of the process is started. Supervision exclusion\ncontinues until the termination of the process. The same principle applies to a change\nin supervision parameters."

      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_73",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00242",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.4: Supervision Exclusion and change of Function Group State\nFigure 7.4 shows an example: If Supervision is excluded in\nFunction Group\nstate-A,\nsame will continue in\nFunction Group\nstate-B. Supervision can be applied again in\nstate-C wherein the process is restarted (but not in state-B).\n[SWS_PHM_00242]\n{DRAFT}\nSupervisions on Restart of Process\n⌈\nSupervisions\non restart of a process due to\nFunction Group\nState change shall be handled as\ntermination of process (see [SWS_PHM_00240]) followed by start of process (see\n[SWS_PHM_00241]).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\n[SWS_PHM_00243]\n{DRAFT}\nContinuation of Supervisions\n⌈\nSupervisions (Alive,\nDeadline and Logical) shall be continued with same values of Supervision parame-\nters if the corresponding process continues to execute on\nFunction Group\nState\nchange.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\n[SWS_PHM_00245]\n{DRAFT}\nContinuation of NoSupervision (Supervision Exclu-\nsion)\n⌈\nIf\nNoSupervision\nis configured for a\nSupervised Entity\nInstance in the\nSupervision Mode\ncorresponding to the\nFunction Group\nState, in which the exe-\ncution of the corresponding process starts, then no Supervision (no\nAlive Supervi-\nsion\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nor\nLogical Supervision\n) shall be continued on\nchange in\nFunction Group\nState to a new state if the process continues to execute\non\nFunction Group\nState change.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00104)\n32 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P33_74",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01342",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5 Determination of Supervision Status\nBased on the results of\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLog-\nical Supervision\nthe\nElementary Supervision Status\nand\nGlobal Su-\npervision Status\nare determined. Please refer [4] for details of these Supervi-\nsions.\n7.5.1 Determination of Elementary Supervision Status\nThe\nElementary Supervision Status\nstate machine determines the status of an\nindividual\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Super-\nvision\n. This is done based on the following:\n1. Previous value of the\nElementary Supervision Status\n,\n2. Current values of the result (correct/incorrect) of the corresponding\nAlive Su-\npervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\nThe state machine is initialized at the initialization of the\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\n. Note: In this release, only state machine for\nElementary Supervision\nStatus\nfor intra process supervision is specified.\n[SWS_PHM_01342]\n{DRAFT}\nTracking of Elementary Supervision Status\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall track the\nElementary Supervision\nStatus\nof each\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical\nSupervision\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nFigure 7.5 shows the state machine for\nElementary Supervision Status\nof a\nsupervision with all possible states.\n[SWS_PHM_01343]\n{DRAFT}\nStates of state machine for Elementary Supervision\nStatus\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall have the\nElementary Super-\nvision Statuses kOK\n,\nkDEACTIVATED\n,\nkEXPIRED\nand\nkFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_-\n00111)\nSee also figure 7.5 and\nara::phm::ElementarySupervisionStatus\n.\nPlease note that the status\nkFAILED\nis only relevant for\nAlive Supervision\n.\n33 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P34_75",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01344",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P34_76",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01344",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.5: Elementary Supervision Status\nFor the transitions between the states of the\nElementary Supervision Status\nthe following rules apply:\n[SWS_PHM_01344]\n{DRAFT}\nInitialization of state machine for Elementary Super-\nvision Status\n⌈\nOn start of\nPlatform Health Management\nall state machines for\nElementary Supervision Status\nshall be initialized to\nkDEACTIVATED\nand for\nAlive Supervision\nthe counter for failed Alive Supervision reference cycles shall\nbe set to zero (0).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (1) in figure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01345]\n{DRAFT}\nKeep Elementary Supervision Status\nkOK\n⌈\nIf the\nEl-\nementary Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\nand the results of the corresponding su-\npervision are correct, i.e. all checkpoints are reported according to configuration and\nin case of\nAlive Supervision\nthe counter for failed Alive Supervision reference cy-\ncles is zero, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall keep the supervision in\nthe\nElementary Supervision Status kOK\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\n[SWS_PHM_01346]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkOK\nto\nkEXPIRED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\nAND in case the\nElementary Supervision Status\ncorresponds to\n1.\nAlive Supervision\na permanent failure is detected, i.e. the counter for failed\nAlive Supervision reference cycles exceeds failure tolerance\nfailedRefer-\nenceCyclesTolerance\n) OR\n34 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P35_77",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01347",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2.\nDeadline Supervision\nor\nLogical Supervision\nthe result of the super-\nvision is incorrect\nTHEN the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\nto\nkEXPIRED\nand stop the corresponding supervision.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_-\n00111)\nSee transition (2) in figure 7.5.\nThe below requirements show the important difference of\nAlive Supervision\nver-\nsus\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\n: the\nAlive Supervi-\nsion\nhas an error tolerance for failed reference cycles.\n[SWS_PHM_01347]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkOK\nto\nkFAILED\n⌈\nIf\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\nAND the corresponding\nsupervision is\nAlive Supervision\nAND a temporary failure is detected, i.e. the\ncounter for failed Alive Supervision reference cycles is greater than zero but does not\nexceed failure tolerance\nfailedReferenceCyclesTolerance\n, THEN the\nPlat-\nform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary Supervision Sta-\ntus\nto\nkFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (3) in figure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01348]\n{DRAFT}\nKeep Elementary Supervision Status\nkFAILED\n⌈\nIf\nthe\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkFAILED\nAND the counter for failed\nAlive Supervision reference cycles is greater than zero but does not exceed fail-\nure tolerance\nfailedReferenceCyclesTolerance\nTHEN the\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nshall keep the\nElementary Supervision Status kFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nPHM_00111)\n[SWS_PHM_01349]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkFAILED\nto\nkOK\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkFAILED\nAND\nthere is no failure present in the\nAlive Supervision\n, i.e. the counter for failed Alive\nSupervision reference cycles is zero, THEN the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary Supervision Status\nto\nkOK\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (5) in figure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01350]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkFAILED\nto\nkEXPIRED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkFAILED\nAND if the\nAlive Supervision\nhas a permanent failure, i.e. the counter for failed\nAlive Supervision reference cycles exceeds failure tolerance\nfailedReferenceCy-\nclesTolerance\n, THEN the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nEl-\nementary Supervision Status\nto\nkEXPIRED\nand stop the corresponding super-\nvision.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (6) in figure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01351]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkOK\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\nAND\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nreceives the information from Execution Management that the\ncorresponding process is about to be notified to terminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n) or the\nprocess is terminated (considering the case of process terminating abruptly, i.e. without\nSIGTERM\nissued by Execution Management), THEN the\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\nshall change the\nElementary Supervision Status\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\n35 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nand for\nAlive Supervision\nthe counter for failed Alive Supervision reference cy-\ncles shall be set to zero (0).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_00104)\nSee transition (7) in\nfigure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01352]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkFAILED\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkFAILED\nAND\nPlatform Health Management\nreceives the information from Ex-\necution Management that the corresponding process is about to be notified to ter-\nminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n) or the process is terminated (considering the case of\nprocess terminating abruptly, i.e. without\nSIGTERM\nissued by Execution Management),\nTHEN the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\nand the counter for failed\nAlive Supervision\nreference cycles shall be set to zero (0).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_00104)\nSee\ntransition (8) in figure 7.5.\n[SWS_PHM_01353]\n{DRAFT}\nKeep Elementary Supervision Status\nkDEACTIVATED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTIVATED\nthen, unless there\nis a switch to a\nSupervision Mode\n(due to change in corresponding\nFunction\nGroup\nState) in which the corresponding supervision is configured to be monitored\nAND\n•\nfor\nAlive Supervision\n: the corresponding Process reports Execution State\nkRunning\n•\nfor\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical Supervision\n: any checkpoint\ncorresponding to the supervision is reported\nthe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall not perform the supervision and keep\nthe\nElementary Supervision Status kDEACTIVATED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_-\nPHM_00104)\n[SWS_PHM_01354]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkDE-\nACTIVATED\nto\nkOK\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTIVATED\nAND there is a switch to a\nSupervision Mode\n(due to change in corresponding\nFunction Group\nState) in which the\nSupervised Entity\nInstance is configured\nto be monitored AND\n•\nfor\nAlive Supervision\n: the corresponding Process reports Execution State\nkRunning\n•\nfor\nDeadline Supervision\n: when first time the checkpoint of the Supervision\nis reported\n•\nfor\nLogical Supervision\n: when first time the checkpoint of the Supervision\nis reported and the supervision result for reporting of this checkpoint is correct\nTHEN\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary Supervi-\nsion Status\nto\nkOK\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_00104)\nSee transition (9) in fig-\nure 7.5.\n36 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P37_79",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01355",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 37,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PHM_01355]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkEX-\nPIRED\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkEX-\nPIRED\nAND the\nElementary Supervision Status\ndoes not correspond to Oper-\nating System, Execution Management or State Management AND\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nreceives the information from Execution Management that the corre-\nsponding process is about to be notified to terminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n) or the pro-\ncess is terminated (considering the case of process terminating abruptly, i.e. without\nSIGTERM\nissued by Execution Management), THEN the\nPlatform Health Man-\nagement\nshall change the\nElementary Supervision Status\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\nand for\nAlive Supervision\nthe counter for failed Alive Supervision reference cy-\ncles shall be set to zero (0).\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_00104)\nSee transition (4) in\nfigure 7.5.\nNote: Transition (4) is not applicable in case of\nElementary Supervision Sta-\ntus\ncorresponding to supervision of Operating System, Execution Management or\nState Management reaches\nkEXPIRED\n. In this case, recovery (state change from\nkEXPIRED\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\n) is intended to be through watchdog action (see\n[SWS_PHM_00105]).\nNote: How to determine whether a supervision corresponds to Execution Manage-\nment/Operating System is not standardized. A relation to State Management can be\ndetermined via the attribute\nfunctionClusterAffiliation\nin the configuration of\nProcess\n:\nConfiguration of Supervisions (\nAliveSupervision\n/\nDeadlineSupervision\n/\nLog-\nicalSupervision\n) have reference to\nSupervisionCheckpoint\nwhich in turn\nrefers\nProcess\nin\nSupervisionCheckpoint\n.\nprocess\n.\nThis\nProcess\ncontains the attribute\nProcess\n.\nfunctionClusterAffilia-\ntion\nand one of the values standardized for this attribute by AUTOSAR is\n\"`STATE_MANAGEMENT\"'. In this way it is possible to Identify which Supervisions\ncorrespond to State Management.\n[SWS_PHM_01356]\n{DRAFT}\nKeep Elementary Supervision Status\nkEXPIRED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkEXPIRED\nthen, unless\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nreceives the information from Execution Management that the\ncorresponding process is about to be notified to terminate (by issuing\nSIGTERM\n) or the\nprocess is terminated (considering the case of process terminating abruptly, i.e. without\nSIGTERM\nissued by Execution Management), the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall not perform the supervision and keep the\nElementary Supervision Status\nkEXPIRED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_00104)\n[SWS_PHM_01357]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Elementary Supervision Status from\nkDEAC-\nTIVATED\nto\nkEXPIRED\n⌈\nIf the\nElementary Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTI-\nVATED\nand it corresponds to\nLogical Supervision\n, when first time the checkpoint\nof the supervision is reported and the supervision result for reporting of this checkpoint\nis incorrect, then\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nElementary\nSupervision Status\nto\nkEXPIRED\nand stop the corresponding supervision.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nPHM_00111)\nSee transition (10) in figure 7.5.\n37 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P38_80",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00105",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: Transition (10) is applicable for\nElementary Supervision Status\nof\nLog-\nical Supervision\nonly.\n7.5.2 Determination of Global Supervision Status\nThe\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis determined based on the\nElementary Su-\npervision Status\nof a set of Alive, Deadline and/or Logical Supervisions within a\nFunction Group\nwhich are configured as part of a single\nGlobalSupervision\n.\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis \"worst-of\" all included\nElementary Supervi-\nsion Statuses\n.\nThe\nGlobal Supervision Status\nhas similar values as the\nElementary Su-\npervision Status\n. The main differences are the addition of the\nkSTOPPED\nvalue.\nFigure 7.6 shows the values and transitions between them.\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nreports a detected failure to State Manage-\nment as soon as state\nkEXPIRED\nis reached. State\nkSTOPPED\nis used only for critical\nfailures which need a direct reaction via hardware watchdog. From AUTOSAR point\nof view, this is relevant for failures in supervisions corresponding to Operating Sys-\ntem, State Management or Execution Management.\nPlatform Health Manage-\nment\ntriggers the watchdog reaction by not setting a correct watchdog trigger condition\nas soon as state\nkSTOPPED\nis reached, see [SWS_PHM_00105]. This transition and\ntherefore the reaction can be postponed for a configurable amount of time, named\nexpiredSupervisionTolerance\n. This could be used to allow clean-up activities\nbefore a watchdog reset, e.g. writing the error cause, writing NVRAM data.\nThe\nexpiredSupervisionTolerance\nis implemented within the state machine of\nthe\nGlobal Supervision Status\n. The defined state machine is in the state\nkEX-\nPIRED\nwhile the error reaction is postponed. Since the transition to state\nkSTOPPED\nis\nonly applicable for supervisions triggering a watchdog reaction, the parameter\nex-\npiredSupervisionTolerance\nis only relevant in this case.\nThat means, it is\nmandatory to configure\nexpiredSupervisionTolerance\nonly in case of Global\nSupervision corresponding to Operating System, State Management or Execu-\ntion Management.\nA constraint in this regard is not added in [13] as Execution Man-\nagement is not a modelled process and Operating System is not represented in the\nmodel.\nA change in\nGlobal Supervision Status\ncan be logged by Platform Health Man-\nagement for test/debugging purposes.\n[SWS_PHM_00219]\n{DRAFT}\nCalculation of Global Supervision Status\n⌈\nThe\nPlat-\nform Health Management\nshall calculate the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nof\neach configured\nGlobalSupervision\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nWhether the evaluation of\nGlobal Supervision Status\nand the\nElementary\nSupervision Status\nthat it aggregates is time triggered (periodic evaluation) or\nevent triggered (on availability of a new result for\nAlive Supervision\n/\nDeadline\n38 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P39_81",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00216",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nSupervision\n/\nLogical Supervision\n) is up to Adaptive Platform Vendor's deci-\nsion.\n[SWS_PHM_00216]\n{DRAFT}\nStates of the state machine for Global Supervision\nStatus\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall have the\nGlobal Supervi-\nsion Statuses kOK\n,\nkDEACTIVATED\n,\nkFAILED\n,\nkEXPIRED\nand\nkSTOPPED\n, see\nara::phm::GlobalSupervisionStatus\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee also figure 7.6."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P39_82",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00216",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.6: Global Supervision Status\n[SWS_PHM_00217]\n{DRAFT}\nOne Global Supervision Status per Global Supervi-\nsion\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall have one\nGlobal Supervision\nStatus\nper\nGlobalSupervision\nconfigured.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\n39 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P40_83",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00218",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 40,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nEach\nGlobalSupervision\nis a set of\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Su-\npervision\nand/or\nLogical Supervision\ncorresponding to a single\nFunction\nGroup\n. There can be one or more\nGlobalSupervision\nper\nFunction Group\n.\nBut a\nGlobalSupervision\ndoes not span across multiple\nFunction Groups\n.\n[SWS_PHM_00218]\n{DRAFT}\nInitialization of Global Supervision Status\n⌈\nThe\nGlobal Supervision Status\nshall be initialized with\nkDEACTIVATED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nPHM_00111)\nSee transition (1) in figure 7.6.\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nprovides a feature to postpone the error re-\naction (the error reaction being not setting a correct watchdog trigger condition) for a\nconfigurable amount of time, named\nexpiredSupervisionTolerance\n.\n[SWS_PHM_00220]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkDEACTI-\nVATED\nto\nkOK\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTIVATED\n, the\nEle-\nmentary Supervision Status\nof at least one Alive, Deadline or Logical Supervi-\nsion is\nkOK\nand no supervision is in\nElementary Supervision Status kFAILED\nor\nkEXPIRED\n, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nGlobal\nSupervision Status\nto\nkOK\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (2) in figure 7.6.\n[SWS_PHM_00221]\n{DRAFT}\nKeep Global Supervision Status\nkOK\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal\nSupervision Status\nis\nkOK\n, the\nElementary Supervision Status\nof at least\none Alive, Deadline or Logical Supervision is\nkOK\nand no supervision is in\nEl-\nementary Supervision Status kFAILED\nor\nkEXPIRED\n, then the\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nshall keep the\nGlobal Supervision Status kOK\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nPHM_00111)\n[SWS_PHM_00222]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkOK\nto\nkDE-\nACTIVATED\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\nor\nkFAILED\nor\nkEX-\nPIRED\nAND the\nElementary Supervision Status\nof all Alive, Deadline and Logi-\ncal Supervisions is\nkDEACTIVATED\n, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall\nset the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nto\nkDEACTIVATED\nand stop measuring Ex-\npired Supervision Time.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transitions (6), (14) and (15) in figure\n7.6.\nThese transitions can occur when State Management has caused change in the state\nof the\nFunction Group\ncorresponding to the Global Supervision such that the Pro-\ncesses corresponding to the\nSupervised Entity\ninstances whose Supervisions\n(\nAlive Supervisions\n,\nDeadline Supervisions\nand/or\nLogical Supervi-\nsions\n) are aggregated in the Global Supervision, are terminated. Typically, this can\noccur due to change in\nFunction Group\nstate to Off state.\n[SWS_PHM_00223]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkOK\nto\nkFAILED\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkOK\n, the\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\nof at least one Alive, Deadline or Logical Supervision is\nkFAILED\nand no supervision is in\nElementary Supervision Status kEXPIRED\n, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nGlobal Supervision Sta-\ntus\nto\nkFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (7) in figure 7.6.\n40 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThis transition can occur when State Management has caused change in the state of\nthe\nFunction Group\ncorresponding to the Global Supervision such that the Process\ncorresponding to the\nSupervised Entity\ninstance whose\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\ncaused the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nto reach state kEX-\nPIRED is terminated or restarted.\n[SWS_PHM_00234]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkEXPIRED\nto\nkFAILED\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkEXPIRED\n, the\nElemen-\ntary Supervision Status\nof at least one Alive, Deadline or Logical Supervision is\nkFAILED\nand no supervision is in\nElementary Supervision Status kEXPIRED\n,\nthen the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nGlobal Supervision\nStatus\nto\nkFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (17) in figure 7.6.\nThis transition can occur when State Management has caused change in the state of\nthe\nFunction Group\ncorresponding to the Global Supervision such that the Process\ncorresponding to the\nSupervised Entity\ninstance whose\nElementary Super-\nvision Status\ncaused the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nto reach state kEX-\nPIRED is terminated or restarted. However, there exists another executing process\nwhose corresponding\nSupervised Entity\ninstance is in\nElementary Supervi-\nsion Status\nkFAILED and is not terminated or restarted.\nNote: Transitions (15), (16) and (17) in figure 7.4 is not applicable in case of\nGlobal-\nSupervision\ncorresponding to Operating System, Execution Management or State\nManagement as\nElementary Supervision Status\nof supervisions correspond-\ning to these is not allowed to leave the state\nkEXPIRED\nuntil watchdog action is taken\n(see [SWS_PHM_00105]).\n[SWS_PHM_00237]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkDEACTI-\nVATED\nto\nkFAILED\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTIVATED\n, the\nElementary Supervision Status\nof at least one Alive, Deadline or Logical Su-\npervision is\nkFAILED\nand no supervision is in\nElementary Supervision Sta-\ntus kEXPIRED\n, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change the\nGlobal\nSupervision Status\nto\nkFAILED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111)\nSee transition (3) in figure\n7.6.\n[SWS_PHM_00238]\n{DRAFT}\nSwitch Global Supervision Status from\nkDEACTI-\nVATED\nto\nkEXPIRED\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\nis\nkDEACTIVATED\n, the\nElementary Supervision Status\nof at least one Alive, Deadline or Logical Su-\npervision is\nkEXPIRED\nand in case the\nGlobalSupervision\ncorresponds to Su-\npervision is\nkEXPIRED\n, the\nexpiredSupervisionTolerance\nis configured to zero\n43 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nand the\nGlobalSupervision\ncorresponds to Operating System, Execution Manage-\nment or State Management, then the\nPlatform Health Management\nshall change\nthe\nGlobal Supervision Status\nto\nkSTOPPED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00111, RS_PHM_-\n00112)\nSee transition (5) in figure 7.6.\nNote: How to distinguish whether a\nGlobalSupervision\ncorresponds to Execution\nManagement/State Management/Operating System is not standardized.\n7.6 Recovery actions\nThe scope of\nPlatform Health Management\nis to monitor the safety relevant\nPro-\ncesses\non the platform and report detect failures to State Management. If a failure in\nState Management is detected,\nPlatform Health Management\ncan trigger a reac-\ntion via hardware watchdog.\n44 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"

    {
