    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P46_90",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00101",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.6.1 Notificaton to State Management\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\ndebounces the failures of\nSupervised En-\ntitys\n, see the\nElementary Supervision Status kFAILED\nin chapter 7.5. After\nthe debouncing, a recovery action is necessary. Thus,\nPlatform Health Manage-\nment\nnotifies State Management. State Management as a coordinator of the platform\ncan decide how a detected failure shall be handled and can trigger corresponding re-\ncovery actions. In most cases this might include switching the faulty\nFunction Group\nto another state.\nAccording to ISO 26262, it has to be ensured that a reaction is triggered after a safety-\nrelevant failure occurred. Therefore,\nPlatform Health Management\nhas to make\nsure that State Management receives the notification on a detected failure. The\nPlat-\nform Health Management\nmonitors the return of the\nRecoveryHandler\nwith a\nconfigurable timeout. If State Management will not regularly return from the\nRecov-\neryHandler\nin time, the PHM will do its own countermeasures by wrongly triggering\nor stop triggering the serviced watchdog.\n[SWS_PHM_00101]\n{DRAFT}\nNotification to State Management due to Supervi-\nsion failure\n⌈\nIf the status of the mapped\nGlobalSupervision\nvia\nRecoveryNoti-\nficationToPPortPrototypeMapping\nswitches to state\nkEXPIRED\n, the Platform\nHealth Management shall notify State Management via the method\nRecoveryHan-\ndler\n. The parameter\nexecutionError\nshall contain the corresponding\nFunction\nGroup\nand the current\nProcessExecutionError\n. The parameter\nsupervision\nshall contain the TypeOfSupervision which causes the transition to state\nkEXPIRED\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09159, RS_HM_09249, RS_PHM_00117)\nNote: A\nGlobalSupervision\ncorresponds to whole or part of a\nFunction Group\n,\ni.e. for each\nGlobalSupervision\nalways the same\nFunction Group\nis reported.\nThe\nProcessExecutionError\nis defined within the\nStartupConfig\n, wherefore the\nexecutionError.executionError depends on the current used\nStartupConfig\n.\n[SWS_PHM_00102]\n{OBSOLETE}\nNotification to State Management due to\nHealth\nStatus\n⌈\nIf the\nHealth Status\nof a\nHealth Channel\nswitches and a reaction of\nState Management is required, i.e.\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\n.\ntriggersRecov-\neryNotification\nequals true for the corresponding\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\n.\nstatusId\n, the Platform Health Management shall notify State Management via the\nmethod\nRecoveryHandler\n. The parameter\nhealthStatusId\nshall be passed from\nthe method\nReportHealthStatus\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09159, RS_HM_09249, RS_PHM_-\n09255)\nThis means that the information about whether a reaction is required has to be config-\nured for\nPlatform Health Management\n.\n[SWS_PHM_00104]\n{DRAFT}\nReaction on timeout for notification to State Man-\nagement\n⌈\nIf after sending a notification on a failure to State Management via the\nmethod\nRecoveryHandler\nno acknowledgment by State Management is received\nbefore\nRecoveryNotification\n.\nrecoveryNotificationTimeout\n,\nPlatform\n46 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P47_91",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01147",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nHealth Management\nshall stop calling\nWatchdogInterface::AliveNotifica-\ntion\nand call\nWatchdogInterface::FireWatchdogReaction\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09159,\nRS_HM_09249, RS_HM_09226)\n[SWS_PHM_01147]\n{DRAFT}\nEnable handler\n⌈\nPlatform Health Management\nshall enable potential invocations of\nRecoveryHandler\nwhen\nOffer\nis called.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nHM_09159)\n[SWS_PHM_01148]\n{DRAFT}\nDisable handler\n⌈\nPlatform Health Management\nshall disable invocations of\nRecoveryHandler\nwhen\nStopOffer\nis called.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nHM_09159)\n7.6.2 Handling of Hardware Watchdog\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nis the only Functional Cluster with an interface\nto the hardware watchdog. Therefore, the watchdog supervises\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nand PHM can initiate a reaction of the watchdog by stop triggering or\nby sending a false trigger. Since this reaction means usually a reset of the machine,\nit has an impact on all functions and should be used only as a last resort in order\nto ensure freedom from interference. Failures that require a watchdog reaction are\nsupervision failures in State Management and Execution Management since in these\ncases a recovery action via State Management as described in section 7.6.1 is not\npossible.\nPlatform Health Management\nhandles the hardware watchdog via the Watch-\ndogInterface. PHM indicates aliveness to WatchdogInterface cyclically. WatchdogIn-\nterface will trigger the hardware watchdog correctly as long as PHM indicates alive-\nness. If PHM does not report aliveness in configured time, WatchdogInterface shall\ninitiate watchdog reaction.\nIn case a critical failure is detected, PHM can trigger recovery action through Watch-\ndogInterface.\n[SWS_PHM_00106]\n{DRAFT}\nRecovery Action for Failures in Execution or State\nManagement\n⌈\nAs long as no\nGlobal Supervision Status\ncorresponding to\nState Management or Execution Management has reached state\nkSTOPPED\nand\nNotification to State Management has not failed,\nPlatform Health Manage-\nment\nshall call\nWatchdogInterface::AliveNotification\nperiodically.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nHM_09249, RS_HM_09226)\n[SWS_PHM_00105]\n{DRAFT}\nRecovery Action for Failures in Execution Manage-\nment or State Management\n⌈\nIf the\nGlobal Supervision Status\ncorresponding\nto State Management or Execution Management switches to\nkSTOPPED\n,\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nshall stop calling\nWatchdogInterface::AliveNotifica-\ntion\nand call\nWatchdogInterface::FireWatchdogReaction\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09249,\nRS_HM_09226, RS_PHM_00115, RS_PHM_00116)\n47 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P48_92",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 48,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.6.3 Configuration Parameters\nConfiguration of recovery actions within\nPlatform Health Management\nhas one\nparameter:\n1.\nrecoveryNotificationTimeout\n: the maximum acceptable amount of time\nPlatform Health Management\nwaits for an acknowledgment by State Man-\nagement after sending the notification.\n48 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P49_93",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 49,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.7 Multiple processes and multiple instances\nDuring the application deployment phase, a single\nSupervised Entity\nor a sin-\ngle\nHealth Channel\nmay be instanciated several times: this happens for example\nwhen the same C++ object class representing a\nSupervised Entity\nor a\nHealth\nChannel\nis explicitly instanciated inside the code or when the same executable con-\ntaining the\nSupervised Entity\nor the\nHealth Channel\nis started/run multiple\ntimes. In such a case, each instance of the\nSupervised Entity\nis individually\nsupervised, each\nAlive Supervision\n,\nDeadline Supervision\nand\nLogical\nSupervision\ngenerating an instance of\nElementary Supervision Status\n.\nA specific instance of a\nSupervised Entity\nor\nHealth Channel\nidentifies itself at\nrun time via an InstanceSpecifier. The API usage of the ara::core::InstanceSpecifier is\nspecified in SWS_CORE_10200 and chapter \"`InstanceSpecifier data type\"' in [8]. The\nmodelling relation of the InstanceSpecifier and its usage in PHM is explained in detail\nin the chapter \"`Supervised Entities and Checkpoints\"' in [13]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P50_94",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01252",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 50,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.8 Functional cluster life-cycle\n7.8.1 Startup\n[SWS_PHM_01252]\n{DRAFT}\nHandling of Watchdog after Startup\n⌈\nPlat-\nform Health Management\nshall call\nWatchdogInterface::AliveNotifi-\ncation\nbefore reporting\nkRunning\nto Execution Management using the\nmethod\nara::exec::ExecutionClient::ReportExecutionState\n.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_-\n09249, RS_HM_09244, RS_HM_09245, RS_HM_09246)\nThe intention is to take over the control of the HW watchdog as early as possible.\nMore information on the machine startup sequence can be found in [11].\n7.8.2 Shutdown\nIt is the integrators responsibility to make correct use of the shutdown mechanism. De-\ntails for ensuring safe execution are given in [14]. Details on the sequence of machine\nshutdown can be found in [11].\n[SWS_PHM_01253]\n{DRAFT}\nTermination of Supervisions at SIGTERM\n⌈\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nshall stop all configured supervisions (eg: delete all supervi-\nsion objects) after receiving SIGTERM.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09222, RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_-\n09235)\n[SWS_PHM_01254]\n{DRAFT}\nGlobal Supervision Status at SIGTERM\n⌈\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nshall change all\nGlobal Supervision Statuses\nto DE-\nACTIVATED after receiving SIGTERM.\n⌋\n(RS_HM_09222, RS_HM_09125, RS_HM_-\n09235)\n7.8.2.1 Handling of watchdog during shutdown\nHandling of watchdog during and after Shutdown of Platform Health Management will\nnot be specified.\nNote: Platform Health Management will no more be able to handle the servicing of the\nwatchdog once it is shutdown.\n50 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P51_95",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01005",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 51,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8 API specification\n8.1 API Header files\nThis section describes the header files of the\nara::phm\nAPI.\nThe generated header files provide the generated types for\nSupervised Entitys\nand\nHealth Channels\n.\n8.1.1\nSupervised Entity\nFor each\nSupervised Entity\n, a separate namespace is generated.\nNamespaces are used to separate the definition of services from each other to prevent\nname conflicts and they allow to use reasonably short names. It is recommended to\ndefine the namespace unique, e.g. by using the company domain name.\n[SWS_PHM_01005] Namespace of generated header files for a\nSupervised En-\ntity\n⌈\nBased on the\nsymbol\nattributes of the ordered\nSymbolProps\naggregated by\nPhmSupervisedEntityInterface\n, the C++ namespace of a\nSupervised En-\ntity\nshall be:\n1\nnamespace ara {\n2\nnamespace phm {\n3\n4\nnamespace supervised_entities {\n5\n6\nnamespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[0].symbol> {\n7\nnamespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[1].symbol> {\n8\nnamespace <...> {\n9\nnamespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[n].symbol> {\n10\n11\nnamespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.shortName> {\n12\n...\n13\n} // namespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.shortName>\n14\n15\n} // namespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[n].symbol>\n16\n} // namespace <...>\n17\n} // namespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[1].symbol>\n18\n} // namespace <PhmSupervisedEntityInterface.namespace[0].symbol>\n19\n20\n} // namespace supervised_entities\n21\n22\n} // namespace phm\n23\n} // namespace ara\nwith all namespace names converted to lower-case letters. These namespaces are\ntaken from\nnamespace\nattribute configured under\nPhmSupervisedEntityInter-\nface\n. Also, see \"Namespace\" under \"Service Interface\" chapter in [13].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_-\n00002)\n51 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P52_96",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01020",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 52,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nSo an example namespace could be e.g.\nara::phm::supervised_entities::oem:body::headlights::low_beam\nwith low_beam being the name of the\nSupervised Entity\nand body, headlights and\nlow_beam are namespaces used to organize and uniquely identify the\nSupervised\nEntity\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01020] Folder structure for\nSupervised Entity\nfiles\n⌈\nThe gener-\nated header files defined by [SWS_PHM_01002] shall be located within the folder:\n<folder>/ara/phm/supervised_entities/<namespace[0]>/.../<namespace[n]>/\nwhere:\n<folder>\nis the start folder for the\nara::phm\nheader files specific for a project or\nplatform vendor,\n<namespace[0]>\n...\n<namespace[n]>\nare the namespace names as defined in\n[SWS_PHM_01005].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00001)\n[SWS_PHM_01002] Generated header files for\nSupervised Entitys\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall provide one\nSupervised Entity\nheader\nfile\nfor each\nPhmSupervisedEntityInterface\ndefined in the input by using the\nfile name\n<name>.h\n, where\n<name>\nis the\nPhmSupervisedEntityInterface\n.\nshortName\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00001)\nSo effectively, for each\nSupervised Entity\n, there is a separate generated file.\nThere can be several\nSupervised Entitys\nin the same namespace, which results\nwith several files in the same folder.\n8.1.2\nHealth Channel\nThe generation of files/namespaces for\nHealth Channels\nis similar to the one of\nSupervised Entitys\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01113]\n{OBSOLETE}\nNamespace of generated header files for a\nHealth Channel\n⌈\nBased on the\nsymbol\nattributes of the ordered\nSymbolProps\naggregated by\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\n, the C++ namespace of the\nHealth\nChannel\nshall be:\n1\nnamespace ara {\n2\nnamespace phm {\n3\nnamespace health_channels {\n4\n5\nnamespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[0].symbol> {\n6\nnamespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[1].symbol> {\n7\nnamespace <...> {\n8\nnamespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[n].symbol> {\n9\n10\nnamespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.shortName> {\n11\n...\n12\n} // namespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.shortName>\n13\n52 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P53_97",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01114",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 53,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n14\n} // namespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[n].symbol>\n15\n} // namespace <...>\n16\n} // namespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[1].symbol>\n17\n} // namespace <PhmHealthChannelInterface.namespace[0].symbol>\n18\n19\n} // namespace health_channels\n20\n21\n} // namespace phm\n22\n} // namespace ara\nwith all namespace names converted to lower-case letters. These namespaces are\ntaken from\nnamespace\nattribute configured under\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\n.\nAlso, see \"Namespace\" under \"Service Interface\" chapter in [13].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00002)\nSo an example namespace could be e.g.\nara::phm::health_channels::oem::drivetrain::wheels:pressure\nwith\npressure\nbeing the name of the\nHealth Channel\nand oem, drivetrain and\nwheels are namespaces used to organize and uniquely identify the\nHealth Channel\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01114]\n{OBSOLETE}\nFolder structure for\nHealth Channel\nfiles\n⌈\nThe\ngenerated header files defined by [SWS_PHM_01002] shall be located within the\nfolder:\n<folder>/ara/phm/health_channels/<namespace[0]>/.../<namespace[n]>/\nwhere:\n<folder>\nis the start folder for the\nara::phm\nheader files specific for a project or\nplatform vendor,\n<namespace[0]>\n...\n<namespace[n]>\nare the namespace names as defined in\n[SWS_PHM_01113].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00001)\n[SWS_PHM_01115]\n{OBSOLETE}\nGenerated header files for\nHealth Channels\n⌈\nThe\nPlatform Health Management\nshall provide one\nHealth Channel\nheader\nfile\nfor each\nHealthChannel\ndefined in the input by using the file name\n<name>.h\n,\nwhere\n<name>\nis the\nHealthChannel\n.\nshortName\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00001)\nSo effectively, for each\nHealth Channel\n, there is a separate generated file. There\ncan be several\nHealth Channels\nin the same namespace, which results with several\nfiles in the same folder.\n8.2 API Common Data Types\nThis chapter describes the standardized types provided by the\nara::phm\nAPI. The\nara::phm\nAPI is based on the\nara::core\ntypes defined in [8].\n53 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P54_98",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00424",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 54,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.2.1 Generated Types\nThis chapter describes the types used by\nPlatform Health Management\nwhich\nare generated dependent on the input configuration.\nAn Enumeration is not a plain primitive data type, but a structural description defined\nwith a set of custom identifiers known as\nenumerators\nrepresenting the possible values.\nIn C++, an enumeration is a first-class object and can take any of these enumerators\nas a value.\n8.2.1.1 Enumeration for\nCheckpoint\nFor each\nSupervised Entity\n, an enumeration is generated containing the corre-\nsponding\nCheckpoints\n.\n[SWS_PHM_00424] Enumeration for\nSupervised Entity\n⌈\nFor each\nPhmSuper-\nvisedEntityInterface\n, there shall exist the corresponding type declaration as:\nenum class Checkpoints : std::uint32_t {\n<enumerator-list>\n};\nwhere\n<enumerator-list>\nare the enumerators as defined by\n[SWS_PHM_00425].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254, RS_-\nPHM_09241)\n[SWS_PHM_00425] Definition of enumerators of\nSupervised Entitys\n⌈\nFor\neach\nPhmCheckpoint\ncontained in the\nPhmSupervisedEntityInterface\n, there\nshall exist the corresponding enumeration nested in the declaration defined by\n[SWS_PHM_00424] as:\n<enumeratorLiteral> = <initializer><suffix>,\nwhere:\n<enumeratorLiteral>\nis\nPhmCheckpoint\n.\nshortName\n<initializer>\nis the\nPhmCheckpoint\n.\ncheckpointId\n<suffix>\nshall be \"U\".\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254, RS_PHM_09241)\nFor example, this can generate:\nenum class Checkpoints : std::uint32_t\n{\nInitializing = 0U,\nStartupTest = 1U,\nInitializingFinished = 2U\n};\n54 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P55_99",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_00426",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PHM_00426] Namespace for\nCheckpoints\n⌈\nThe enumeration contain-\ning\nCheckpoints\nspecified in [SWS_PHM_00424] shall be generated in the\nnamespace of the corresponding\nPhmSupervisedEntityInterface\ndescribed\nin [SWS_PHM_01005].\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254, RS_-\nPHM_09241)\n8.2.1.2 Enumeration for\nHealth Status\nThe generation for\nHealth Channels\nis similar to the one of\nSupervised Enti-\ntys\n.\nFor each\nHealth Channel\n, an enumeration is generated containing the correspond-\ning\nHealth Statuses\n.\n[SWS_PHM_01118]\n{OBSOLETE}\nEnumeration for\nHealth Channel\n⌈\nFor each\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\n, there shall exist the corresponding type declaration\nas:\nenum class HealthStatuses : uint32_t {\n<enumerator-list>\n};\nwhere\n<enumerator-list>\nare the enumerators as defined by [SWS_PHM_01119]\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00102, RS_PHM_09257)\n[SWS_PHM_01119]\n{OBSOLETE}\nDefinition of enumerators of\nHealth Channels\n⌈\nFor each\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\ncontained in the\nPhmHealthChannelIn-\nterface\n, there shall exist the corresponding enumeration nested in the declaration\ndefined by [SWS_PHM_01118] as:\n<enumeratorLiteral> = <initializer><suffix>,\nwhere:\n<enumeratorLiteral>\nis\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\n.\nshortName\n<initializer>\nis the\nPhmHealthChannelStatus\n.\nstatusId\n<suffix>\nshall be \"U\".\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00102, RS_PHM_09257)\nFor example, this can generate:\nenum class HealthStatuses : uint32_t\n{\nLow = 0U,\nHigh = 1U,\nOk = 2U,\nVeryLow = 3U,\nVeryHigh = 4U\n};\n55 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_phm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P56_100",
      "source_element": "SWS_PHM_01129",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement",
      "source_page": 56,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PHM_01129]\n{OBSOLETE}\nEnumeration for\nHealth Channel\n⌈\nThe enu-\nmeration containing\nHealth Statuses\nspecified in [SWS_PHM_01118] shall be\ngenerated in the namespace of the corresponding\nPhmHealthChannelInterface\ndescribed in [SWS_PHM_01113]\n⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00102, RS_PHM_-\n09257)\n8.2.2 Non-generated types\nThis section defines the types that are non-generated.\n8.2.2.1 ElementarySupervisionStatus\n[SWS_PHM_01358]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API enum ara::phm::ElementarySuper-\nvisionStatus\n⌈"

      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_PHM_00003)\n8.2.2.8 Daisy Chaining Related Types (Non-generated)\nDaisy chaining\nis not supported in this AUTOSAR release.\n8.2.2.9 Error and Exception Types\nThe ara::phm API does not explicitly make use of C++ exceptions. The AUTOSAR\nimplementer is free to provide an exception-free implementation or an implementation\nthat uses Unchecked Exceptions. The implementer is however not allowed to define\nChecked Exceptions.\nara::phm API builds upon a clean separation of exception types into Unchecked Ex-\nceptions and Checked Exceptions.\nThe former ones (i.e., Unchecked Exceptions) can basically occur in\nany\nara::phm API\ncall, are not formally modeled in the Manifest, and are fully implementation specific.\nThe latter ones (i.e., Checked Exceptions) are not used by Health Management API.\n8.2.2.10 E2E Related Data Types\nThe usage of E2E communication protection for Health Management is not standard-\nized.\n59 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },

      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3 API Reference\n8.3.1 SupervisedEntity API\nSupervisedEntity\nAPI can be used to report\nCheckpoint\ns or to query the status\nof a\nSupervisedEntity\n.\n8.3.1.1 SupervisedEntity::SupervisedEntity\n[SWS_PHM_01123] Definition of API function ara::phm::SupervisedEn-\ntity::SupervisedEntity\n⌈"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nB.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces\nwhich are accessible by user space applications (see chapters 8 and 9) can also be\nused for interaction between Functional Clusters.\nThe goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-\nteraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between\ndocuments specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-\ntion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform\nprovider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.\n89 of 99 Document ID 851: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Platform Health Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nC Platform Extension API (normative)\nThe focus of the APIs in this section are for OEM-specific platform extensions. The\nabstraction of the interfaces is lower which could lead to a higher machine dependency.\nC.1 WatchdogInterface\nThis chapter lists the required APIs for PHM to interact with the hardware watchdog.\nC.1.1 WatchdogInterface::AliveNotification"

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h3>Rolle &amp; Verwendungszweck</h3><p>Der Functional Cluster Platform Health Management (<code>ara::phm</code>) überwacht das korrekte zeitliche und logische Ausführungsverhalten von Prozessen und Softwarekomponenten auf der AUTOSAR Adaptive Plattform <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#page=12\">SWS Platform Health Management §1 „Introduction and functional overview“</a>. Als zentrale Sicherheits- und Zuverlässigkeitsinstanz stellt PHM sicher, dass Rechenzeitüberschreitungen, Programmabstürze, Endlosschleifen oder fehlerhafte Kontrollflüsse frühzeitig erkannt und durch deterministische Recovery-Maßnahmen oder Hardware-Watchdog-Eskalationen abgefangen werden <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00101\">[SWS_PHM_00101]</a>.</p><p>Das Modul aggregiert lokale Kontrollpunktmeldungen von sogenannten <em>Supervised Entities</em>, bewertet diese anhand formal modellierter Überwachungsregeln und leitet bei Abweichungen abgestufte Reaktionen ein. Hierzu gehören die Benachrichtigung der betroffenen Anwendung oder des State Managements zur Initiierung von Wiederanläufen oder Funktionsgruppenwechseln sowie bei kritischen Systemfehlern die Ansteuerung physischer Watchdogs <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00231\">[SWS_PHM_00231]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01229\">[SWS_PHM_01229]</a>.</p><h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3><p>Die Architektur von <code>ara::phm</code> trennt strikt zwischen der Instrumentierung in den Anwendungs-Prozessen und der zentralen Auswertungslogik im PHM-Dämon <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#page=14\">SWS Platform Health Management §7 „Functional specification“</a>:</p><ul><li><strong>Supervised Entity (<code>ara::phm::SupervisedEntity</code>):</strong> Repräsentiert ein softwaremäßiges Überwachungsobjekt (z. B. einen Prozess, einen Thread oder eine kritische Funktionsschleife). Die Anwendung instanziiert <code>SupervisedEntity</code> über einen im Manifest definierten <code>InstanceSpecifier</code> und meldet das Erreichen von Kontrollpunkten über <code>ReportCheckpoint(checkpointId)</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00104\">[SWS_PHM_00104]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00425\">[SWS_PHM_00425]</a>. Diese Aufrufe sind lock-frei und minimalinvasiv gestaltet, um deterministisches Laufzeitverhalten zu gewährleisten.</li><li><strong>Drei Überwachungsmechanismen (Elementary Supervisions):</strong> PHM bewertet Checkpoints anhand dreier komplementärer Kriterien:\n    <ul>\n      <li><em>Alive Supervision:</em> Prüft, ob ein Checkpoint innerhalb eines definierten Referenzzeitraums mit einer erwarteten Mindest- und Höchstfrequenz gemeldet wird (Erkennung von Thread-Blockaden oder unkontrolliertem Durchlaufen) <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01123\">[SWS_PHM_01123]</a>.</li>\n      <li><em>Deadline Supervision:</em> Misst die Latenzzeit zwischen zwei definierten Checkpoints (z. B. Beginn und Ende einer Bildverarbeitungsroutine) und detektiert Fristüberschreitungen oder unzulässig frühe Ausführungen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01127\">[SWS_PHM_01127]</a>.</li>\n      <li><em>Logical Supervision:</em> Verifiziert die Einhaltung eines zulässigen Kontrollflussgraphen (Transitionen zwischen Checkpoints), um unzulässige Sprünge oder übersprungene Initialisierungen abzufangen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01141\">[SWS_PHM_01141]</a>.</li>\n    </ul>\n  </li><li><strong>Status-Aggregation &amp; Funktionsgruppen-Kontext:</strong> Jede elementare Überwachung besitzt einen lokalen <em>Elementary Supervision Status</em>. Diese werden innerhalb eines Function-Group-Kontexts über ein Worst-of-Prinzip zu einem <em>Global Supervision Status</em> verdichtet <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00216\">[SWS_PHM_00216]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00218\">[SWS_PHM_00218]</a>. Befindet sich eine Funktionsgruppe im Zustand <code>NoSupervision</code>, werden eingehende Checkpoints ignoriert <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01142\">[SWS_PHM_01142]</a>.</li><li><strong>Recovery Action (<code>ara::phm::RecoveryAction</code>):</strong> Schnittstelle zur Entkopplung von Fehlererkennung und Fehlerreaktion. Registrierte Handler empfangen Benachrichtigungen bei Zustandsübergängen auf <code>kEXPIRED</code> und leiten Wiederanläufe oder Fallback-Betriebsmodi ein <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01333\">[SWS_PHM_01333]</a>.</li></ul><h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3><p>Der Interaktionsfluss beginnt mit dem Melden von Kontrollpunkten durch die Supervised Entity. PHM aktualisiert intern die Zähler, Zeitstempel und Graphzustände. Solange alle Prüfungen innerhalb der Toleranzbänder liegen, verbleibt der Globalstatus in <code>kOK</code>. Bei einer Verletzung wechselt der Status auf <code>kFAILED</code> bzw. nach Ablauf konfigurierter Fehlertoleranzen auf <code>kEXPIRED</code>, was den Recovery-Handler aktiviert. Führt dies zu keiner Wiederherstellung oder betrifft der Fehler das Basis-Betriebssystem bzw. Execution Management, wechselt der Status auf <code>kSTOPPED</code> und löst die Watchdog-Eskalation aus.</p><div class=\"diagram\" id=\"diag-01\"><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" viewbox=\"0 class=\"diagram-note\">Interaktionsdiagramm: Zyklische Checkpoint-Meldung durch eine Supervised Entity, interne Bewertung (Alive/Deadline/Logical), Benachrichtigung der RecoveryAction bei Statusübergang nach kEXPIRED und abschließende Watchdog-Eskalation bei anhaltendem kSTOPPED. Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00425\">[SWS_PHM_00425]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00231\">[SWS_PHM_00231]</a> und <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01229\">[SWS_PHM_01229]</a>.</p><h3>Konfiguration &amp; Fehlerbehandlung</h3><p>Die Parametrierung erfolgt deklarativ im AUTOSAR-Manifest über <code>PlatformHealthManagementContribution</code>. Dort werden Checkpoints, Zeitschranken (Min/Max-Deadlines in Mikrosekunden), Alive-Toleranzzyklen, zulässige Graphübergänge sowie die Zuordnung von Supervised Entities zu Function Groups konfiguriert <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4\">SWS Platform Health Management §7.4 „Determination of Supervision Status“</a>.</p><p>Die Zustandsmaschine des Global Supervision Status unterscheidet fünf deterministische Zustände <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00216\">[SWS_PHM_00216]</a>:</p><ul><li><code>kDEACTIVATED</code>: Die Überwachung ist für die aktuelle Funktionsgruppe nicht aktiv.</li><li><code>kOK</code>: Alle elementaren Überwachungen erfüllen ihre Spezifikationsgrenzen.</li><li><code>kFAILED</code>: Mindestens eine Überwachung hat einen Fehler detektiert, befindet sich aber noch innerhalb der konfigurierten Fehlertoleranzschwelle (z. B. einzelne ausgelassene Alive-Meldung).</li><li><code>kEXPIRED</code>: Die Fehlertoleranz wurde überschritten; die Überwachung ist abgelaufen. Dieser Zustand löst unmittelbar die hinterlegte <code>RecoveryAction</code> aus <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00231\">[SWS_PHM_00231]</a>.</li><li><code>kSTOPPED</code>: Terminaler Fehlerzustand, wenn Recovery-Maßnahmen fehlschlagen oder Kernprozesse (EM/OS) betroffen sind. In diesem Zustand wird der Hardware-Watchdog nicht mehr getriggert, was einen kontrollierten System-Reset einleitet <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01229\">[SWS_PHM_01229]</a>.</li></ul></div>\n",

<div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Supervision als Plattform-Sicherheitsfunktion</h4><p>Platform Health Management bewertet das zeitliche und logische Verhalten von Supervised Entities mit Alive-, Deadline- und Logical-Supervision. Eine Supervised Entity steht für einen ganzen Prozess oder einen Teil davon und meldet die im Code definierten Checkpoints <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=chapter.7">SWS Platform Health Management §7 „Functional specification“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS PHM §7.2 „Supervision of Supervised Entities“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/FO/AUTOSAR_FO_RS_HealthMonitoring.pdf#page=6">RS Health Monitoring (Foundation), Supervision-Arten (S. 6)</a>.</p><h4>Von Checkpoints zu einer Function-Group-Aussage</h4><p>Jede Alive-, Deadline- oder Logical-Supervision hat einen Elementary Supervision Status. Die manifest-konfigurierte Menge dieser Status innerhalb eines Function-Group-Kontexts ergibt als Worst-of-Aggregation einen Global Supervision Status. Eine Elementarsupervision gehört dabei nur einer Global Supervision <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS PHM §7.4 „Determination of Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.4.2">SWS PHM §7.4.2 „Determination of Global Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#page=11">RS Platform Health Management, Statusaggregation (S. 11)</a>.</p><div href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS PHM §7.2 „Supervision of Supervised Entities“</a> <a class="docref" kritische Eskalation</h4><p>Der Globalstatus beginnt in <code>kDEACTIVATED</code> und kennt zusätzlich <code>kOK</code>, <code>kFAILED</code>, <code>kEXPIRED</code> und <code>kSTOPPED</code>. <code>kEXPIRED</code> löst für nicht grundlegende Cluster die Recovery-Benachrichtigung aus; bei EM-, SM- oder OS-bezogener Supervision kann nach der konfigurierten Toleranz <code>kSTOPPED</code> und damit der Watchdog-Pfad folgen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00216">[SWS_PHM_00216]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00231">[SWS_PHM_00231]</a>.</p><div class="diagram" </div><p class="diagram-note">Zustandsdiagramm: Der globale Status aggregiert die Elementarstatus und enthält <code>kSTOPPED</code> für den kritischen Watchdog-Pfad <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.4.2">SWS PHM §7.4.2 „Determination of Global Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.2">SWS PHM §7.5.2 „Handling of Hardware Watchdog“</a>. <em>Interpretation: Nicht alle in der Spezifikation einzeln ausgeführten Rückwege sind dargestellt.</em></p><h4>Recovery mit State Management und Watchdog</h4><p>Bei einer abgelaufenen Global Supervision benachrichtigt PHM State Management über <code>RecoveryAction::RecoveryHandler</code>. Bleibt dessen Antwort aus, wird Recovery als nicht behandelbar signalisiert oder betrifft der Fehler EM beziehungsweise SM, stoppt PHM die Watchdog-Aliveness und fordert eine Reaktion an <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.5">SWS PHM §7.5 „Recovery actions“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.2">SWS PHM §7.5.2 „Handling of Hardware Watchdog“</a>.</p><h4>Modus- und Lifecycle-Kopplung</h4><p>Der Supervision Mode hängt am Function-Group-Zustand. Alive-Supervision startet nach der <code>kRunning</code>-Meldung von EM; Deadline- und Logical-Supervision können prozessintern vorher beginnen. Beim Terminieren eines Prozesses werden die zugehörigen Supervisionen gestoppt <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS PHM §7.3 „Supervision Modes“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01331">[SWS_PHM_01331]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01333">[SWS_PHM_01333]</a>.</p><h4>API-Nachweise</h4><p>Die folgenden bereits verknüpften API- und Quellennachweise bleiben für die Detailverfolgung erhalten: <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_phm_SupervisedEntity_c46882.html#SWS_PHM_01127">[SWS_PHM_01127]</a>, <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../namespaces/ns_phm_ara_phm_supervised_entities_hierarchical_namespace_list_8fbd5f.html#SWS_PHM_00425">[SWS_PHM_00425]</a>, <a class="docref vis-internal" href="../classes/cl_ara_phm_RecoveryAction_8b27fd.html">RecoveryAction</a>, <a class="swsref vis-internal" href="../classes/cl_ara_phm_RecoveryAction_8b27fd.html#SWS_PHM_01142">[SWS_PHM_01142]</a>, <a <div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Supervision als Plattform-Sicherheitsfunktion</h4><p>Platform Health Management bewertet das zeitliche und logische Verhalten von Supervised Entities mit Alive-, Deadline- und Logical-Supervision. Eine Supervised Entity steht für einen ganzen Prozess oder einen Teil davon und meldet die im Code definierten Checkpoints <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=chapter.7">SWS Platform Health Management §7 „Functional specification“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS PHM §7.2 „Supervision of Supervised Entities“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/FO/AUTOSAR_FO_RS_HealthMonitoring.pdf#page=6">RS Health Monitoring (Foundation), Supervision-Arten (S. 6)</a>.</p><h4>Von Checkpoints zu einer Function-Group-Aussage</h4><p>Jede Alive-, Deadline- oder Logical-Supervision hat einen Elementary Supervision Status. Die manifest-konfigurierte Menge dieser Status innerhalb eines Function-Group-Kontexts ergibt als Worst-of-Aggregation einen Global Supervision Status. Eine Elementarsupervision gehört dabei nur einer Global Supervision <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS PHM §7.4 „Determination of Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.4.2">SWS PHM §7.4.2 „Determination of Global Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#page=11">RS Platform Health Management, Statusaggregation (S. 11)</a>.</p><div kritische Eskalation</h4><p>Der Globalstatus beginnt in <code>kDEACTIVATED</code> und kennt zusätzlich <code>kOK</code>, <code>kFAILED</code>, <code>kEXPIRED</code> und <code>kSTOPPED</code>. <code>kEXPIRED</code> löst für nicht grundlegende Cluster die Recovery-Benachrichtigung aus; bei EM-, SM- oder OS-bezogener Supervision kann nach der konfigurierten Toleranz <code>kSTOPPED</code> und damit der Watchdog-Pfad folgen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_00216">[SWS_PHM_00216]</a> <a fill="#28251d">Watchdog-Pfad</text> </g> </g> </svg> </div><p class="diagram-note">Zustandsdiagramm: Der globale Status aggregiert die Elementarstatus und enthält <code>kSTOPPED</code> für den kritischen Watchdog-Pfad <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.4.2">SWS PHM §7.4.2 „Determination of Global Supervision Status“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.2">SWS PHM §7.5.2 „Handling of Hardware Watchdog“</a>. <em>Interpretation: Nicht alle in der Spezifikation einzeln ausgeführten Rückwege sind dargestellt.</em></p><h4>Recovery mit State Management und Watchdog</h4><p>Bei einer abgelaufenen Global Supervision benachrichtigt PHM State Management über <code>RecoveryAction::RecoveryHandler</code>. Bleibt dessen Antwort aus, wird Recovery als nicht behandelbar signalisiert oder betrifft der Fehler EM beziehungsweise SM, stoppt PHM die Watchdog-Aliveness und fordert eine Reaktion an <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.5">SWS PHM §7.5 „Recovery actions“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.2">SWS PHM §7.5.2 „Handling of Hardware Watchdog“</a>.</p><h4>Modus- und Lifecycle-Kopplung</h4><p>Der Supervision Mode hängt am Function-Group-Zustand. Alive-Supervision startet nach der <code>kRunning</code>-Meldung von EM; Deadline- und Logical-Supervision können prozessintern vorher beginnen. Beim Terminieren eines Prozesses werden die zugehörigen Supervisionen gestoppt <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS PHM §7.3 „Supervision Modes“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01331">[SWS_PHM_01331]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformHealthManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PHM_01333">[SWS_PHM_01333]</a>.</p><h4>API-Nachweise</h4><p>Die folgenden bereits verknüpften API- und Quellennachweise bleiben für die Detailverfolgung erhalten: <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_phm_SupervisedEntity_c46882.html#SWS_PHM_01127">[SWS_PHM_01127]</a>, Specification of Platform Health Management
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
1 Introduction and functional overview
This document is the software specification of the
Platform Health Management
functional cluster within the Adaptive Platform [1].
The specification implements the requirements specified in [2, RS Platform Health
Management].
It also implements the general functionality described in the Foundation documents [3,
RS Health Monitoring] and [4, ASWS Health Monitoring]. In addition to the functionality
specified in [4], this document also defines
Health Channel Supervision
.
Health Monitoring
is required by [5, ISO 26262:2018] (under the terms control flow
monitoring, external monitoring facility, watchdog, logical monitoring, temporal moni-
toring, program sequence monitoring) and this specification is supposed to address all
relevant requirements from this standard.

Specification of Platform Health Management
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
4 Constraints and assumptions
4.1 Known limitations
•
Daisy chaining
(i.e. forwarding Supervision Status,
Checkpoint
or
Health
Channel
information to an entity external to PHM or another PHM instance) is
currently not supported in this document release.
•
Interface with the Diagnostic Manager is not specified in this release.
•
Health Channels
(HealthChannelExternalStatus) is set to obsolete.
Note: It is not intended to remove this feature from
AUTOSAR Adaptive Plat-
form
overall. Rather, it is an architectural question to which Functional Cluster
this feature belongs to, that is expected to be resolved for the next release.
•
The configuration attribute for the alive notification cycle time (with respect to
PHM sending AliveNotification to watchdog interface) is not specified for this re-
lease.
•
A change in the value of Supervision (Alive/Deadline/Logical) configuration pa-
rameters between two
Function Group
states wherein the process being su-
pervised continues to execute on switching between these states is not con-
sidered. The Supervision continues as per configuration in the
Supervision
Mode
corresponding to old
Function Group
state.
•
Similar to above limitation, dynamic change between Supervision exclusion (dis-
able) and Supervision inclusion (enable) on
Function Group
state change
wherein the process under consideration continues to execute on change in
Function Group
state is not supported. Supervision exclusion or inclusion
can be applied starting with the
Function Group
state in which execution of
the process begins and the same is applied until termination of the process.
•
Currently specified mechanism of Notifying State Management on
Global Su-
pervision Status
reaching state
kStopped
is insufficient in case of multiple
failures. It could happen that the
Global Supervision Status
remains in
state
kStopped
without further notification to State Management about succes-
sive failures. Thereby the recovery might be hindered.
•
"PowerMode" dependent Supervision configuration is not supported in this re-
lease. See [9] for information on "PowerMode".
•
Supervision is not supported for non-reporting processes (for information regard-
ing what is a non-reporting process, please refer [10]). Rationale: Supervision
depends on process states. Non-reporting process is not expected to report its
Execution State to Execution Management. Hence,
Platform Health Man-
agement
cannot be informed about the necessary process states by Execution
Management.
•
Handling of multiple hardware watchdog instances is up to implementation and
not standardized in the specification.

Specification of Platform Health Management
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
7 Functional specification
7.1 General description
The
Platform Health Management
monitors applications with respect to tim-
ing constraints (
Alive Supervision
and
Deadline Supervision
) and logical
program sequence (
Logical Supervision
) as well as platform health (
Health
Channel Supervision
). In case of a detected failure,
Platform Health Man-
agement
notifies State Management. As coordinator of the platform, State Manage-
ment can decide how to handle the error and trigger a suitable recovery action.
Platform Health Management has also an interface to the hardware watchdog and can
trigger a watchdog reaction in case of a critical failure where a notification to State
Management is not sufficient.
All the algorithms and the procedures for the
Platform Health Management
are
described in the Autosar Foundation document [4] and are not specified here: only the
Autosar Adaptive specificities, including the interfaces with the other functional clusters,
are shown here below.
The interfaces of Health Management to other Functional Clusters are only informative
and are not standardized.
7.2 Supervision of Supervised Entities
State Management coordinates the platform through Function Groups [9]. Within a
Function Group, there may be multiple
Processes
running.
Platform Health Management
monitors
Supervised Entitys
. Each
Super-
vised Entity
maps to whole or part of a
Process
. The monitoring is active as long
as the corresponding
Process
is active.
Platform Health Management
provides three kinds of supervisions to monitor
a
Supervised Entity
:
Alive Supervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Logical Supervision
. The supervision algorithms are described in [4]. Only de-
tails specific for Adaptive Platform are described in this document.
The results of the supervisions of a
Supervised Entity
Instance are reflected in
the
Elementary Supervision Status
.There exists one
Elementary Super-
vision Status
per Alive, Deadline, Logical Supervision. The status of elemen-
tary supervisions within a
Function Group
is conglomerated in the corresponding
Global Supervision Status
.
One
Elementary Supervision Status
contributes to only one
Global Super-
vision Status
. Which
Elementary Supervision Status
contributes to which
Global Supervision Status
is determined by to which Global Supervision the
corresponding supervision belongs to in the Manifest.

Specification of Platform Health Management
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
Scope of Global Supervision: Global Supervision corresponds to whole or part of a
Function Group
. A Global Supervision can contain all or a certain set of Elementary
Supervisions corresponding to processes controlled within a single Function Group
context. The mapping from Supervisions to Global Supervision is flexible. Through
configuration, user can decide which Supervisions belong to which Global Supervision.
But there are following restrictions:
•
all Supervisions comprising a Global Supervision are corresponding to processes
controlled within a single Function Group context and
•
a Supervision can be part of only one Global Supervision.

7.2.1.1 Stopping of Alive Supervision for Self Terminating Process
In case of a Self-Terminating Process, the process can intentionally terminate even
without
SIGTERM
being issued by Execution Management. Hence, it is necessary to
mark the point in time at which the process starts to (self-) terminate so that the
Alive
Supervision
could be stopped. This is intended to be achieved by process reporting
a checkpoint named as
terminatingCheckpoint
. Additionally, a timeout (config-
urable) has to be monitored by
Platform Health Management
to check that the
process terminates within this duration since reporting of
terminatingCheckpoint
.
This timeout check is to monitor that the process is not stuck in its execution and there-
fore is not terminating.
Note: Unless
SIGTERM
is issued to the process by Execution Management, Execution
Management will not monitor for process termination timeout.
Platform Health Management
is to be informed by Execution Management re-
garding the termination of the process.

Process

shall be

terminatingCheckpoint
by the process or as soon as
Platform Health Management
receives the information from Execution Manage-

AUTOSAR AP R23-11

Health Management

A
Health Channel
can be
•
the Global supervision status of the software under supervision.
•
the result of an environment monitoring algorithm. e.g. Voltage Monitoring, Tem-
perature Monitoring.
•
the result of a memory integrity test routine, e.g. RAM test, ROM test.
•
the status of the operating system or Kernel. e.g. OS Status, Kernel Status.
•
the status of another platform instance or Virtual Machine or ECU.
The various external monitoring routines shall report their result or status in the form of
defined
Health Statuses
to the
Platform Health Management
. The
Health
Status
of a
Health Channel
is the abstract format of the information that a
Health
Channel
provides to the
Platform Health Management
. Two different
Health
Channels
may have same
Health Status
names to represent its result, e.g. high,
low, normal.
If a reaction on a determined
Health Status
is necessary,
Platform Health
Management
reports the status to State Management.
7.3.1 Health Status after Initialization
The
Health Status
after initialization is controlled by the configuration container
HealthStatusInitValue
. This parameter may be configured once for each
Health Channel
in the configuration.

{OBSOLETE}
Not initialized Health Channel
⌈
If the container
HealthStatusInitValue
does not exist or the
Health Channel
does not already
have an initial value, the
Platform Health Management
shall treat the correspond-
ing
Health Status
as undefined and not use it until the corresponding
Health
Channel
has been updated for the first time.
⌋
(RS_PHM_09255, RS_HM_09249)

ID

3.

: Initial value of the corresponding Health Status.

7.4 Supervision Modes
Expected execution (timing or sequence) of the Software can change based on certain
conditions. Hence, the value of the Supervision (Alive/Deadline/Logical) parameters
might have to be changed based on conditions. For each such condition a mode called
a
Supervision Mode
can be configured. Currently, this condition can be configured
based on
Function Group
State.

In

Function Group State change has following impact on processes:
•
Certain processes are terminated.
•

•
Certain processes are restarted.
•
Remaining processes continue to execute.
Supervisions (Alive, Deadline and Logical) of the
Supervised Entitys
correspond-
ing to the processes shall be handled as follows.

The termination of the process could be due to various reasons. It could be due to
change in
Function Group
State (the process is not configured to be executed in
the new
Function Group
State), a self-terminating process is terminating on its own
or abrupt termination of a process (e.g. due to out of bound memory access).

1. On termination of process,
Elementary Supervision Status
of the corre-
sponding
Supervised Entity
Instance will be set to
kDEACTIVATED
.
2. For a process, monitoring is active when the process is executing (that is, when
the Execution state of the process is "Initializing" or "Running" or "Terminating").
It is deactivated (stopped) when the process is terminated.

State,

,

values in the

On start of the
process in the new
Function Group
State, if

is configured for

7.5 Determination of Supervision Status
Based on the results of
Alive Supervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Log-
ical Supervision
the
Elementary Supervision Status
and
Global Su-
pervision Status
are determined. Please refer [4] for details of these Supervi-
sions.
7.5.1 Determination of Elementary Supervision Status
The
Elementary Supervision Status
state machine determines the status of an
individual
Alive Supervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Logical Super-
vision
. This is done based on the following:
1. Previous value of the
Elementary Supervision Status
,
2. Current values of the result (correct/incorrect) of the corresponding
Alive Su-
pervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Logical Supervision
The state machine is initialized at the initialization of the
Platform Health Man-
agement
. Note: In this release, only state machine for
Elementary Supervision
Status
for intra process supervision is specified.
[SWS_PHM_01342]
{DRAFT}
Tracking of Elementary Supervision Status
⌈
The
Platform Health Management
shall track the
Elementary Supervision
Status
of each
Alive Supervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Logical
Supervision
.
⌋
(RS_PHM_00111)
Figure 7.5 shows the state machine for
Elementary Supervision Status
of a
supervision with all possible states.
[SWS_PHM_01343]
{DRAFT}
States of state machine for Elementary Supervision
Status
⌈
The
Platform Health Management
shall have the
Elementary Super-
vision Statuses kOK
,
kDEACTIVATED
,
kEXPIRED
and
kFAILED
.
⌋
(RS_PHM_-
00111)
See also figure 7.5 and
ara::phm::ElementarySupervisionStatus
.
Please note that the status
kFAILED
is only relevant for
Alive Supervision
.

AUTOSAR AP R23-11
Note: Transition (10) is applicable for

ical Supervision

7.5.2 Determination of Global Supervision Status
The
Global Supervision Status
is determined based on the
Elementary Su-
pervision Status
of a set of Alive, Deadline and/or Logical Supervisions within a
Function Group
which are configured as part of a single
GlobalSupervision
.
Global Supervision Status
is "worst-of" all included
Elementary Supervi-
sion Statuses
.
The
Global Supervision Status
has similar values as the
Elementary Su-
pervision Status
. The main differences are the addition of the
kSTOPPED
value.
Figure 7.6 shows the values and transitions between them.
The
Platform Health Management
reports a detected failure to State Manage-
ment as soon as state
kEXPIRED
is reached. State
kSTOPPED
is used only for critical
failures which need a direct reaction via hardware watchdog. From AUTOSAR point
of view, this is relevant for failures in supervisions corresponding to Operating Sys-
tem, State Management or Execution Management.
Platform Health Manage-
ment
triggers the watchdog reaction by not setting a correct watchdog trigger condition
as soon as state
kSTOPPED
is reached, see [SWS_PHM_00105]. This transition and
therefore the reaction can be postponed for a configurable amount of time, named
expiredSupervisionTolerance
. This could be used to allow clean-up activities
before a watchdog reset, e.g. writing the error cause, writing NVRAM data.
The
expiredSupervisionTolerance
is implemented within the state machine of
the
Global Supervision Status
. The defined state machine is in the state
kEX-
PIRED
while the error reaction is postponed. Since the transition to state
kSTOPPED
is
only applicable for supervisions triggering a watchdog reaction, the parameter
ex-
piredSupervisionTolerance
is only relevant in this case.
That means, it is
mandatory to configure
expiredSupervisionTolerance
only in case of Global
Supervision corresponding to Operating System, State Management or Execu-
tion Management.
A constraint in this regard is not added in [13] as Execution Man-
agement is not a modelled process and Operating System is not represented in the
model.
A change in
Global Supervision Status
can be logged by Platform Health Man-
agement for test/debugging purposes.
[SWS_PHM_00219]
{DRAFT}
Calculation of Global Supervision Status
⌈
The
Plat-
form Health Management
shall calculate the
Global Supervision Status
of
each configured
GlobalSupervision
.

7.6 Recovery actions
The scope of
Platform Health Management
is to monitor the safety relevant
Pro-
cesses
on the platform and report detect failures to State Management. If a failure in
State Management is detected,
Platform Health Management
can trigger a reac-
tion via hardware watchdog.

7.6.1 Notificaton to State Management
The
Platform Health Management
debounces the failures of
Supervised En-
titys
, see the
Elementary Supervision Status kFAILED
in chapter 7.5. After
the debouncing, a recovery action is necessary. Thus,
Platform Health Manage-
ment
notifies State Management. State Management as a coordinator of the platform
can decide how a detected failure shall be handled and can trigger corresponding re-
covery actions. In most cases this might include switching the faulty
Function Group
to another state.
According to ISO 26262, it has to be ensured that a reaction is triggered after a safety-
relevant failure occurred. Therefore,
Platform Health Management
has to make
sure that State Management receives the notification on a detected failure. The
Plat-
form Health Management
monitors the return of the
RecoveryHandler
with a
configurable timeout. If State Management will not regularly return from the
Recov-
eryHandler
in time, the PHM will do its own countermeasures by wrongly triggering
or stop triggering the serviced watchdog.

RecoveryHan-
dler
. The parameter
executionError
shall contain the corresponding
Function
Group
and the current
ProcessExecutionError
. The parameter
supervision
shall contain the TypeOfSupervision which causes the transition to state
kEXPIRED
.
⌋
(RS_HM_09159, RS_HM_09249, RS_PHM_00117)
Note: A
GlobalSupervision
corresponds to whole or part of a
Function Group
,
i.e. for each
GlobalSupervision
always the same
Function Group
is reported.
The
ProcessExecutionError
is defined within the
StartupConfig
, wherefore the
executionError.executionError depends on the current used
StartupConfig
.

7.6.2 Handling of Hardware Watchdog
The
Platform Health Management
is the only Functional Cluster with an interface
to the hardware watchdog. Therefore, the watchdog supervises
Platform Health
Management
and PHM can initiate a reaction of the watchdog by stop triggering or
by sending a false trigger. Since this reaction means usually a reset of the machine,
it has an impact on all functions and should be used only as a last resort in order
to ensure freedom from interference. Failures that require a watchdog reaction are
supervision failures in State Management and Execution Management since in these
cases a recovery action via State Management as described in section 7.6.1 is not
possible.
Platform Health Management
handles the hardware watchdog via the Watch-
dogInterface. PHM indicates aliveness to WatchdogInterface cyclically. WatchdogIn-
terface will trigger the hardware watchdog correctly as long as PHM indicates alive-
ness. If PHM does not report aliveness in configured time, WatchdogInterface shall
initiate watchdog reaction.
In case a critical failure is detected, PHM can trigger recovery action through Watch-
dogInterface.
[SWS_PHM_00106]
{DRAFT}
Recovery Action for Failures in Execution or State
Management
⌈
As long as no
Global Supervision Status
corresponding to
State Management or Execution Management has reached state
kSTOPPED
and
Notification to State Management has not failed,
Platform Health Manage-
ment
shall call
WatchdogInterface::AliveNotification
periodically.
⌋
(RS_-
HM_09249, RS_HM_09226)
[SWS_PHM_00105]
{DRAFT}
Recovery Action for Failures in Execution Manage-
ment or State Management
⌈
If the
Global Supervision Status
corresponding
to State Management or Execution Management switches to
kSTOPPED
,
Platform
Health Management
shall stop calling
WatchdogInterface::AliveNotifica-
tion
and call
WatchdogInterface::FireWatchdogReaction
.
⌋
(RS_HM_09249,
RS_HM_09226, RS_PHM_00115, RS_PHM_00116)

7.7 Multiple processes and multiple instances
During the application deployment phase, a single
Supervised Entity
or a sin-
gle
Health Channel
may be instanciated several times: this happens for example
when the same C++ object class representing a
Supervised Entity
or a
Health
Channel
is explicitly instanciated inside the code or when the same executable con-
taining the
Supervised Entity
or the
Health Channel
is started/run multiple
times. In such a case, each instance of the
Supervised Entity
is individually
supervised, each
Alive Supervision
,
Deadline Supervision
and
Logical
Supervision
generating an instance of
Elementary Supervision Status
.
A specific instance of a
Supervised Entity
or
Health Channel
identifies itself at
run time via an InstanceSpecifier. The API usage of the ara::core::InstanceSpecifier is
specified in [SWS_CORE_10200] and chapter "`InstanceSpecifier data type"' in [8]. The
modelling relation of the InstanceSpecifier and its usage in PHM is explained in detail
in the chapter "`Supervised Entities and Checkpoints"' in [13].

7.8.2 Shutdown
It is the integrators responsibility to make correct use of the shutdown mechanism. De-
tails for ensuring safe execution are given in [14]. Details on the sequence of machine
shutdown can be found in [11].

7.8.2.1 Handling of watchdog during shutdown
Handling of watchdog during and after Shutdown of Platform Health Management will
not be specified.
Note: Platform Health Management will no more be able to handle the servicing of the
watchdog once it is shutdown.

8.1.1

For each

Namespaces are used to separate the definition of services from each other to prevent
name conflicts and they allow to use reasonably short names. It is recommended to
define the namespace unique, e.g. by using the company domain name.

8.2.1 Generated Types
This chapter describes the types used by
Platform Health Management
which
are generated dependent on the input configuration.
An Enumeration is not a plain primitive data type, but a structural description defined
with a set of custom identifiers known as
enumerators
representing the possible values.
In C++, an enumeration is a first-class object and can take any of these enumerators
as a value.
8.2.1.1 Enumeration for
Checkpoint
For each
Supervised Entity
, an enumeration is generated containing the corre-
sponding
Checkpoints
.
[SWS_PHM_00424] Enumeration for
Supervised Entity
⌈
For each
PhmSuper-
visedEntityInterface
, there shall exist the corresponding type declaration as:
enum class Checkpoints : std::uint32_t {

};
where

are the enumerators as defined by
[SWS_PHM_00425].
⌋
(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254, RS_-
PHM_09241)
[SWS_PHM_00425] Definition of enumerators of
Supervised Entitys
⌈
For
each
PhmCheckpoint
contained in the
PhmSupervisedEntityInterface
, there
shall exist the corresponding enumeration nested in the declaration defined by
[SWS_PHM_00424] as:
= ,
where:

is
PhmCheckpoint
.
shortName

is the
PhmCheckpoint
.
checkpointId

shall be "U".
⌋
(RS_PHM_00003, RS_PHM_00101, RS_HM_09254, RS_PHM_09241)
For example, this can generate:
enum class Checkpoints : std::uint32_t
{
Initializing = 0U,
StartupTest = 1U,
InitializingFinished = 2U
};

8.2.2.8 Daisy Chaining Related Types (Non-generated)
Daisy chaining
is not supported in this AUTOSAR release.
8.2.2.9 Error and Exception Types
The ara::phm API does not explicitly make use of C++ exceptions. The AUTOSAR
implementer is free to provide an exception-free implementation or an implementation
that uses Unchecked Exceptions. The implementer is however not allowed to define
Checked Exceptions.
ara::phm API builds upon a clean separation of exception types into Unchecked Ex-
ceptions and Checked Exceptions.
The former ones (i.e., Unchecked Exceptions) can basically occur in
any
ara::phm API
call, are not formally modeled in the Manifest, and are fully implementation specific.
The latter ones (i.e., Checked Exceptions) are not used by Health Management API.
8.2.2.10 E2E Related Data Types
The usage of E2E communication protection for Health Management is not standard-
ized.

B Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)
B.1 Overview
AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between
Functional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which
might depend e.g. on the used Operating System.
This chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional
Clusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe
Inter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces
which are accessible by user space applications (see chapters 8 and 9) can also be
used for interaction between Functional Clusters.
The goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-
teraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between
documents specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-
tion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform
provider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.
